```sql
WITH expression AS (
    SELECT
        "case_barcode",
        LOG(10, AVG("normalized_count")) AS log_expression
    FROM TCGA_HG19_DATA_V0.TCGA_HG19_DATA_V0.RNASEQ_GENE_EXPRESSION_UNC_RSEM
    WHERE "HGNC_gene_symbol" = 'TP53'
      AND "project_short_name" = 'TCGA-BRCA'
      AND "normalized_count" > 0
    GROUP BY "case_barcode"
),

mutations AS (
    SELECT
        "case_barcode",
        "Variant_Classification"
    FROM TCGA_HG19_DATA_V0.TCGA_HG19_DATA_V0.SOMATIC_MUTATION_MC3
    WHERE "Hugo_Symbol" = 'TP53'
      AND "project_short_name" = 'TCGA-BRCA'
),

combined AS (
    SELECT
        m."Variant_Classification" AS variant_type,
        e.log_expression
    FROM mutations m
    INNER JOIN expression e
        ON m."case_barcode" = e."case_barcode"
),

grand_stats AS (
    SELECT
        COUNT(*) AS total_n,
        AVG(log_expression) AS grand_mean
    FROM combined
),

group_stats AS (
    SELECT
        variant_type,
        COUNT(*) AS n_j,
        AVG(log_expression) AS group_mean
    FROM combined
    GROUP BY variant_type
),

ss_within AS (
    SELECT
        c.variant_type,
        SUM(POWER(c.log_expression - gs.group_mean, 2)) AS ss_within
    FROM combined c
    JOIN group_stats gs ON c.variant_type = gs.variant_type
    GROUP BY c.variant_type
),

anova_components AS (
    SELECT
        (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM group_stats) AS k,
        MAX(grand_stats.total_n) AS N,
        SUM(group_stats.n_j * POWER(group_stats.group_mean - grand_stats.grand_mean, 2)) AS SSB,
        SUM(ss_within.ss_within) AS SSW
    FROM group_stats, grand_stats, ss_within
    WHERE group_stats.variant_type = ss_within.variant_type
)

SELECT
    N AS "total_number_of_samples",
    k AS "number_of_mutation_types",
    ROUND(SSB / (k - 1), 4) AS "mean_square_between",
    ROUND(SSW / (N - k), 4) AS "mean_square_within",
    ROUND((SSB / (k - 1)) / NULLIF(SSW / (N - k), 0), 4) AS "F_statistic"
FROM anova_components;
```
</details>

<details>
<summary><b>View SlayQL SQL (❌)</b></summary>

```sql
WITH
-- Step 1: Get TP53 expression for TCGA-BRCA (positive counts only, one value per case)
tp53_expression AS (
    SELECT DISTINCT
        e."case_barcode",
        e."normalized_count"
    FROM TCGA_HG19_DATA_V0.TCGA_HG19_DATA_V0.RNASEQ_GENE_EXPRESSION_UNC_RSEM e
    WHERE e."HGNC_gene_symbol" = 'TP53'
      AND e."project_short_name" = 'TCGA-BRCA'
      AND e."normalized_count" > 0
      AND e."normalized_count" IS NOT NULL
),

-- Step 2: Get TP53 mutation types for TCGA-BRCA, aggregated per case
-- If a case has multiple different mutation types, concatenate them sorted
tp53_mutation_groups AS (
    SELECT
        m."case_barcode",
        LISTAGG(DISTINCT m."Variant_Classification", ', ')
            WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY m."Variant_Classification") AS mutation_group
    FROM TCGA_HG19_DATA_V0.TCGA_HG19_DATA_V0.SOMATIC_MUTATION_MC3 m
    WHERE m."Hugo_Symbol" = 'TP53'
      AND m."project_short_name" = 'TCGA-BRCA'
    GROUP BY m."case_barcode"
),

-- Step 3: Combine expression with mutation group
-- Cases without TP53 mutation get group 'WT' (wild-type)
combined AS (
    SELECT
        LOG10(e."normalized_count") AS log_expression,
        COALESCE(mg.mutation_group, 'WT') AS mutation_group
    FROM tp53_expression e
    LEFT JOIN tp53_mutation_groups mg
        ON e."case_barcode" = mg."case_barcode"
),

-- Step 4: Grand statistics (across all samples)
grand_stats AS (
    SELECT
        COUNT(*) AS N,
        AVG(log_expression) AS grand_mean
    FROM combined
),

-- Step 5: Per-group statistics
group_stats AS (
    SELECT
        mutation_group,
        COUNT(*) AS n_j,
        AVG(log_expression) AS mean_j
    FROM combined
    GROUP BY mutation_group
),

-- Step 6: Number of groups
k_val AS (
    SELECT COUNT(*) AS k FROM group_stats
),

-- Step 7: Compute SSB = SUM(n_j * (mean_j - grand_mean)^2)
ssb AS (
    SELECT SUM(g.n_j * POWER(g.mean_j - gr.grand_mean, 2)) AS SSB
    FROM group_stats g, grand_stats gr
),

-- Step 8: Compute SSW = SUM of squared deviations within each group
ssw AS (
    SELECT SUM(POWER(c.log_expression - g.mean_j, 2)) AS SSW
    FROM combined c
    JOIN group_stats g ON c.mutation_group = g.mutation_group
)

-- Step 9: Final ANOVA results
SELECT
    gr.N                                                                   AS total_samples,
    k.k                                                                    AS num_mutation_types,
    ROUND(ssb.SSB / (k.k - 1), 4)                                          AS mean_square_between,
    ROUND(ssw.SSW / (gr.N - k.k), 4)                                       AS mean_square_within,
    ROUND((ssb.SSB / (k.k - 1)) / NULLIF(ssw.SSW / (gr.N - k.k), 0), 4)    AS f_statistic
FROM grand_stats gr, k_val k, ssb, ssw;
```

#### 📜 Generated SQL Queries

<details>
<summary><b>View Baseline SQL (❌)</b></summary>

```sql
WITH 
-- Step 1: Filter KIRP patients with non-null clinical_stage
kirp_patients AS (
    SELECT "case_barcode", "clinical_stage"
    FROM "TCGA_HG38_DATA_V0"."TCGA_BIOCLIN_V0"."CLINICAL"
    WHERE "disease_code" = 'KIRP' 
      AND "clinical_stage" IS NOT NULL
      AND "clinical_stage" != 'None'
),

-- Step 2: Get expression data for the three genes
gene_expression AS (
    SELECT 
        e."case_barcode",
        e."gene_name",
        e."HTSeq__FPKM_UQ"
    FROM "TCGA_HG38_DATA_V0"."TCGA_HG38_DATA_V0"."RNASEQ_GENE_EXPRESSION" e
    INNER JOIN kirp_patients p ON e."case_barcode" = p."case_barcode"
    WHERE e."gene_name" IN ('MT-CO3', 'MT-CO1', 'MT-CO2')
),

-- Step 3: Pivot expression data to one row per patient
pivoted_expression AS (
    SELECT 
        "case_barcode",
        MAX(CASE WHEN "gene_name" = 'MT-CO3' THEN "HTSeq__FPKM_UQ" END) AS "mt_co3",
        MAX(CASE WHEN "gene_name" = 'MT-CO1' THEN "HTSeq__FPKM_UQ" END) AS "mt_co1",
        MAX(CASE WHEN "gene_name" = 'MT-CO2' THEN "HTSeq__FPKM_UQ" END) AS "mt_co2"
    FROM gene_expression
    GROUP BY "case_barcode"
),

-- Step 4: Assign split using HASH (Snowflake equivalent of FARM_FINGERPRINT)
patient_split AS (
    SELECT 
        p."case_barcode",
        p."clinical_stage",
        e."mt_co3",
        e."mt_co1",
        e."mt_co2",
        CASE 
            WHEN MOD(ABS(HASH(p."case_barcode")), 10) < 9 THEN 'train'
            ELSE 'test'
        END AS "split"
    FROM kirp_patients p
    INNER JOIN pivoted_expression e ON p."case_barcode" = e."case_barcode"
),

-- Step 5: Calculate stage averages in training set
stage_averages AS (
    SELECT 
        "clinical_stage",
        AVG("mt_co3") AS "avg_mt_co3",
        AVG("mt_co1") AS "avg_mt_co1",
        AVG("mt_co2") AS "avg_mt_co2"
    FROM patient_split
    WHERE "split" = 'train'
    GROUP BY "clinical_stage"
),

-- Step 6: For each test patient, compute Euclidean distance to each stage average
test_patient_distances AS (
    SELECT 
        t."case_barcode",
        s."clinical_stage",
        SQRT(
            POWER(t."mt_co3" - s."avg_mt_co3", 2) +
            POWER(t."mt_co1" - s."avg_mt_co1", 2) +
            POWER(t."mt_co2" - s."avg_mt_co2", 2)
        ) AS "distance"
    FROM patient_split t
    CROSS JOIN stage_averages s
    WHERE t."split" = 'test'
),

-- Step 7: Assign each test patient to the closest stage
ranked_predictions AS (
    SELECT 
        "case_barcode",
        "clinical_stage",
        ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY "case_barcode" ORDER BY "distance" ASC) AS "rn"
    FROM test_patient_distances
)

-- Final output
SELECT 
    "case_barcode",
    "clinical_stage" AS "predicted_clinical_stage"
FROM ranked_predictions
WHERE "rn" = 1
ORDER BY "case_barcode";
```
</details>

<details>
<summary><b>View SlayQL SQL (❌)</b></summary>

```sql
WITH
-- Step 1: Select eligible KIRP patients with non-null clinical stage
eligible_patients AS (
    SELECT DISTINCT
        c."case_barcode",
        c."case_gdc_id",
        c."clinical_stage"
    FROM "TCGA_HG38_DATA_V0"."TCGA_BIOCLIN_V0"."CLINICAL" c
    WHERE c."disease_code" = 'KIRP'
      AND c."clinical_stage" IS NOT NULL
      AND c."clinical_stage" != 'None'
),

-- Step 2: Randomly split patients into training (90%) and test (10%) sets
-- using hash-based fingerprint on case_barcode
patient_split AS (
    SELECT
        "case_barcode",
        "case_gdc_id",
        "clinical_stage",
        CASE WHEN ABS(HASH("case_barcode")) % 100 < 90 THEN 'train' ELSE 'test' END AS "split"
    FROM eligible_patients
),

-- Step 3: Join with RNAseq expression data for the three target genes
-- Aggregate per patient per gene to handle multiple samples/aliquots
patient_gene_expression AS (
    SELECT
        p."case_barcode",
        p."clinical_stage",
        p."split",
        e."gene_name",
        AVG(e."HTSeq__FPKM_UQ") AS "expr_value"
    FROM patient_split p
    JOIN "TCGA_HG38_DATA_V0"."TCGA_HG38_DATA_V0"."RNASEQ_GENE_EXPRESSION" e
        ON p."case_gdc_id" = e."case_gdc_id"
    WHERE e."gene_name" IN ('MT-CO3', 'MT-CO1', 'MT-CO2')
    GROUP BY p."case_barcode", p."clinical_stage", p."split", e."gene_name"
),

-- Step 4: Calculate average expression per gene per clinical stage in training set
training_stage_averages AS (
    SELECT
        "clinical_stage",
        "gene_name",
        AVG("expr_value") AS "avg_expr"
    FROM patient_gene_expression
    WHERE "split" = 'train'
    GROUP BY "clinical_stage", "gene_name"
),

-- Step 5: Pivot training averages to one column per gene
stage_avg_pivot AS (
    SELECT
        "clinical_stage",
        MAX(CASE WHEN "gene_name" = 'MT-CO1' THEN "avg_expr" END) AS "avg_MT_CO1",
        MAX(CASE WHEN "gene_name" = 'MT-CO2' THEN "avg_expr" END) AS "avg_MT_CO2",
        MAX(CASE WHEN "gene_name" = 'MT-CO3' THEN "avg_expr" END) AS "avg_MT_CO3"
    FROM training_stage_averages
    GROUP BY "clinical_stage"
),

-- Step 6: Pivot test patient expression to one row per patient
test_patient_pivot AS (
    SELECT
        "case_barcode",
        MAX(CASE WHEN "gene_name" = 'MT-CO1' THEN "expr_value" END) AS "expr_MT_CO1",
        MAX(CASE WHEN "gene_name" = 'MT-CO2' THEN "expr_value" END) AS "expr_MT_CO2",
        MAX(CASE WHEN "gene_name" = 'MT-CO3' THEN "expr_value" END) AS "expr_MT_CO3"
    FROM patient_gene_expression
    WHERE "split" = 'test'
    GROUP BY "case_barcode"
),

-- Step 7: Cross join test patients with all stage averages,
-- compute Euclidean distance between patient expression and each stage average
patient_distances AS (
    SELECT
        tp."case_barcode",
        sa."clinical_stage",
        SQRT(
            POWER(tp."expr_MT_CO1" - sa."avg_MT_CO1", 2) +
            POWER(tp."expr_MT_CO2" - sa."avg_MT_CO2", 2) +
            POWER(tp."expr_MT_CO3" - sa."avg_MT_CO3", 2)
        ) AS "euclidean_distance"
    FROM test_patient_pivot tp
    CROSS JOIN stage_avg_pivot sa
),

-- Step 8: For each test patient, rank stages by distance and pick the closest
ranked_predictions AS (
    SELECT
        "case_barcode",
        "clinical_stage",
        ROW_NUMBER() OVER (
            PARTITION BY "case_barcode"
            ORDER BY "euclidean_distance" ASC
        ) AS "rn"
    FROM patient_distances
)

-- Step 9: Final output - case_barcode and the predicted clinical stage
SELECT
    "case_barcode",
    "clinical_stage" AS "predicted_clinical_stage"
FROM ranked_predictions
WHERE "rn" = 1
ORDER BY "case_barcode";
```
</details>

```sql
WITH
-- Step 1: Identify patients from Annotations with exclusion criteria
excluded_patients AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT case_gdc_id
  FROM `isb-cgc.TCGA_bioclin_v0.Annotations`
  WHERE entity_type = 'Patient'
    AND (category = 'History of unacceptable prior treatment related to a prior/other malignancy'
         OR classification = 'Redaction')
),

-- Step 2: Identify target cohort: female, BRCA, age <= 30
target_patients AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT case_gdc_id, case_barcode
  FROM `isb-cgc.TCGA_bioclin_v0.Clinical`
  WHERE disease_code = 'BRCA'
    AND age_at_diagnosis <= 30
    AND gender = 'FEMALE'
),

-- Step 3: FULL JOIN and keep patients where annotation fields are NULL (not excluded)
valid_patients AS (
  SELECT t.case_gdc_id, t.case_barcode
  FROM target_patients t
  FULL JOIN excluded_patients e ON t.case_gdc_id = e.case_gdc_id
  WHERE e.case_gdc_id IS NULL
)

-- Step 4: Get GDC file URLs from rel14 metadata
SELECT DISTINCT
  vp.case_barcode,
  -- Construct GDC file URL using file_gdc_id from the GCS URL mapping table
  CONCAT('https://api.gdc.cancer.gov/data/', g.file_gdc_id) AS gdc_file_url
FROM valid_patients vp
JOIN `isb-cgc.GDC_metadata.rel14_caseData` cd 
  ON vp.case_gdc_id = cd.case_gdc_id
JOIN `isb-cgc.GDC_metadata.rel14_fileData_current` fdc 
  ON cd.case_gdc_id = fdc.case_gdc_id
JOIN `isb-cgc.GDC_metadata.rel14_GDCfileID_to_GCSurl_NEW` g 
  ON fdc.file_gdc_id = g.file_gdc_id
ORDER BY vp.case_barcode;
```

```sql
annotation_cases AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT case_barcode
  FROM `isb-cgc.TCGA_bioclin_v0.Annotations`
  WHERE entity_type = 'Patient'
    AND (
      LOWER(category) LIKE LOWER('%History of unacceptable prior treatment related to a prior/other malignancy%')
      OR LOWER(classification) LIKE LOWER('%Redaction%')
    )
),

-- Identify eligible clinical patients: BRCA, female, age <= 30
clinical_cases AS (
  SELECT 
    case_barcode,
    case_gdc_id
  FROM `isb-cgc.TCGA_bioclin_v0.Clinical`
  WHERE disease_code = 'BRCA'
    AND age_at_diagnosis <= 30
    AND gender = 'FEMALE'
),

-- FULL JOIN - keep only patients from clinical who have no matching annotation
valid_cases AS (
  SELECT 
    c.case_barcode,
    c.case_gdc_id
  FROM annotation_cases a
  FULL JOIN clinical_cases c
    ON a.case_barcode = c.case_barcode
  WHERE a.case_barcode IS NULL  
    AND c.case_barcode IS NOT NULL
)

-- Map valid cases to file GDC IDs and then to GCS URLs
SELECT 
  v.case_barcode,
  u.file_gdc_id AS gdc_file_url
FROM valid_cases v
INNER JOIN `isb-cgc.GDC_metadata.rel14_fileData_current` f
  ON v.case_gdc_id = f.case_gdc_id
INNER JOIN `isb-cgc.GDC_metadata.rel14_GDCfileID_to_GCSurl_NEW` u
  ON f.file_gdc_id = u.file_gdc_id
ORDER BY v.case_barcode
```
</details>

```sql
-- Step 1: Identify BRCA patients and their histological types from clinical table
WITH brca_patients AS (
    SELECT DISTINCT
        c."bcr_patient_barcode" AS "ParticipantBarcode",
        c."histological_type" AS "histological_type"
    FROM
        "PANCANCER_ATLAS_1"."PANCANCER_ATLAS_FILTERED"."CLINICAL_PANCAN_PATIENT_WITH_FOLLOWUP_FILTERED" c
    WHERE

),

)

ORDER BY
```

#### 📜 Generated SQL Queries

<details>
<summary><b>View Baseline SQL (❌)</b></summary>

```sql
WITH
  -- Step 1: Get imaging Level2 data at HTAN WUSTL excluding unwanted components and electron microscopy
  level2 AS (
    SELECT DISTINCT
      Imaging_Assay_Type,
      HTAN_Data_File_ID
    FROM `isb-cgc-bq.HTAN_versioned.imaging_level2_metadata_r5`
    WHERE
      HTAN_Center = 'HTAN WUSTL'
      AND Component IS NOT NULL
      AND Component NOT LIKE '%Auxiliary%'
      AND Component NOT LIKE '%OtherAssay%'
      AND Imaging_Assay_Type NOT LIKE '%Electron%'
  ),

  -- Step 2: Trace to higher-level data files using id_provenance_r5 (parent-child by HTAN_Data_File_ID)
  provenance_children AS (
    SELECT DISTINCT
      l2.Imaging_Assay_Type,
      prov.HTAN_Data_File_ID AS child_data_file_id
    FROM level2 l2
    INNER JOIN `isb-cgc-bq.HTAN_versioned.id_provenance_r5` prov
      ON l2.HTAN_Data_File_ID = prov.HTAN_Parent_Data_File_ID
  ),

  -- Step 3: Identify which children exist in Level3 (imaging_level3_segmentation_metadata_r5)
  level3 AS (
    SELECT DISTINCT child_data_file_id
    FROM provenance_children
    WHERE child_data_file_id IN (
      SELECT HTAN_Data_File_ID
      FROM `isb-cgc-bq.HTAN_versioned.imaging_level3_segmentation_metadata_r5`
      WHERE Component IS NOT NULL
        AND Component NOT LIKE '%Auxiliary%'
        AND Component NOT LIKE '%OtherAssay%'
    )
  ),

  -- Step 4: Identify which children exist in Level4 (imaging_level4_metadata_r5)
  level4 AS (
    SELECT DISTINCT child_data_file_id
    FROM provenance_children
    WHERE child_data_file_id IN (
      SELECT HTAN_Data_File_ID
      FROM `isb-cgc-bq.HTAN_versioned.imaging_level4_metadata_r5`
      WHERE Component IS NOT NULL
        AND Component NOT LIKE '%Auxiliary%'
        AND Component NOT LIKE '%OtherAssay%'
    )
  ),

  -- Step 5: Aggregate per imaging assay type to determine presence of Level3 and Level4
  level_presence AS (
    SELECT
      pc.Imaging_Assay_Type,
      MAX(CASE WHEN l3.child_data_file_id IS NOT NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS has_level3,
      MAX(CASE WHEN l4.child_data_file_id IS NOT NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS has_level4
    FROM provenance_children pc
    LEFT JOIN level3 l3 ON pc.child_data_file_id = l3.child_data_file_id
    LEFT JOIN level4 l4 ON pc.child_data_file_id = l4.child_data_file_id
    GROUP BY pc.Imaging_Assay_Type
  )

-- Final output: list imaging assay types and the available levels
SELECT
  l2.Imaging_Assay_Type,
  CONCAT(
    'Level2',
    IF(lp.has_level3 = 1, ', Level3', ''),
    IF(lp.has_level4 = 1, ', Level4', '')
  ) AS available_data_levels
FROM (SELECT DISTINCT Imaging_Assay_Type FROM level2) l2
LEFT JOIN level_presence lp ON l2.Imaging_Assay_Type = lp.Imaging_Assay_Type
ORDER BY l2.Imaging_Assay_Type;
```
</details>

<details>
<summary><b>View SlayQL SQL (❌)</b></summary>

```sql
-- Step 1: Identify Level2 imaging data at HTAN WUSTL with proper Component and no Electron Microscopy
WITH level2 AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT
    Imaging_Assay_Type,
    HTAN_Data_File_ID,
    entityId
  FROM `isb-cgc-bq.HTAN_versioned.imaging_level2_metadata_r5`
  WHERE HTAN_Center = 'HTAN WUSTL'
    AND Component IS NOT NULL
    AND Component NOT LIKE '%Auxiliary%'
    AND Component NOT LIKE '%OtherAssay%'
    AND Imaging_Assay_Type NOT LIKE '%Electron%'
),

-- Step 2: Link Level2 files to their children via id_provenance_r5
provenance AS (
  SELECT
    Parent.HTAN_Data_File_ID AS parent_file_id,
    Child.entityId AS child_entity_id
  FROM `isb-cgc-bq.HTAN_versioned.id_provenance_r5` AS Child
  INNER JOIN level2 AS Parent
    ON Child.HTAN_Parent_Data_File_ID = Parent.HTAN_Data_File_ID
),

-- Step 3: Identify children that are Level3 imaging files
level3_exists AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT parent_file_id
  FROM provenance
  WHERE child_entity_id IN (
    SELECT entityId
    FROM `isb-cgc-bq.HTAN_versioned.imaging_level3_segmentation_metadata_r5`
  )
),

-- Step 4: Identify children that are Level4 imaging files
level4_exists AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT parent_file_id
  FROM provenance
  WHERE child_entity_id IN (
    SELECT entityId
    FROM `isb-cgc-bq.HTAN_versioned.imaging_level4_metadata_r5`
  )
)

-- Step 5: Aggregate per assay type and show available levels
SELECT
  l2.Imaging_Assay_Type,
  CONCAT(
    'Level2',
    IF(COUNT(DISTINCT l3.parent_file_id) > 0, ', Level3', ''),
    IF(COUNT(DISTINCT l4.parent_file_id) > 0, ', Level4', '')
  ) AS available_data_levels
FROM level2 l2
LEFT JOIN level3_exists l3
  ON l3.parent_file_id = l2.HTAN_Data_File_ID
LEFT JOIN level4_exists l4
  ON l4.parent_file_id = l2.HTAN_Data_File_ID
GROUP BY l2.Imaging_Assay_Type
-- Only include assay types that have at least one higher-level (Level3 or Level4) data
HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT l3.parent_file_id) > 0
    OR COUNT(DISTINCT l4.parent_file_id) > 0
ORDER BY l2.Imaging_Assay_Type;
```
</details>

```sql
  GROUP BY "FEATURE_NAME"
)
```

```sql
-- Compute Pearson correlation between Mitelman DB and TCGA frequencies
-- for copy number aberrations (amplifications, gains, losses, deletions)
-- in breast cancer cases (morph=3111, topo=0401).
-- Results are returned per chromosome and aberration type,
-- only including groups with at least 5 matching cytobands.

WITH
  -- total number of distinct Mitelman cases meeting the criteria
  total_cases AS (
    SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT CONCAT(CAST(RefNo AS STRING), '_', CaseNo)) AS cnt
    FROM `mitelman-db.prod.Cytogen`
    WHERE Morph = '3111' AND Topo = '0401'
  ),

  -- get all valid investigation numbers for each case (needed to join with CytoConverted)
  mitelman_cases_inv AS (
    SELECT c.RefNo, c.CaseNo, i.InvNo
    FROM `mitelman-db.prod.Cytogen` c
    INNER JOIN `mitelman-db.prod.CytogenInv` i
      ON c.RefNo = i.RefNo AND c.CaseNo = i.CaseNo
    WHERE c.Morph = '3111' AND c.Topo = '0401'
  ),

  -- count number of distinct Mitelman cases per cytoband and aberration type
  -- using CytoConverted coordinates overlapping hg38 cytobands
  mitelman_count AS (
    SELECT
      chr.chromosome,
      chr.cytoband_name,
      CASE
        WHEN cc.Type = 'Gain' THEN 'Gain'
        WHEN cc.Type = 'Loss' THEN 'Loss'
        WHEN cc.Type = 'Amplification' THEN 'Amplification'
        WHEN cc.Type = 'Deletion' THEN 'Deletion'
        ELSE 'Unknown'
      END AS aberration_type,
      COUNT(DISTINCT CONCAT(CAST(cc.RefNo AS STRING), '_', cc.CaseNo)) AS case_count
    FROM `mitelman-db.prod.CytoBands_hg38` chr
    INNER JOIN `mitelman-db.prod.CytoConverted` cc
      ON cc.Chr = chr.chromosome
         AND cc.Start < chr.hg38_stop
         AND cc.End > chr.hg38_start
    INNER JOIN mitelman_cases_inv mci
      ON cc.RefNo = mci.RefNo
         AND cc.CaseNo = mci.CaseNo
         AND cc.InvNo = mci.InvNo
    WHERE cc.Type IN ('Gain', 'Loss', 'Amplification', 'Deletion')
    GROUP BY chromosome, cytoband_name, aberration_type
  ),

  -- convert counts to frequencies (percentage of total cases)
  mitelman_freq AS (
    SELECT
      chromosome,
      cytoband_name,
      aberration_type,
      SAFE_DIVIDE(case_count, (SELECT cnt FROM total_cases)) * 100 AS freq
    FROM mitelman_count
  ),

  -- Compute TCGA frequencies for BRCA samples
  tcga_total_samples AS (
    SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT sample_id) AS cnt
    FROM `isb-cgc.tcga_2019_02.Copy_Number_Segment`
    WHERE project_id = 'TCGA-BRCA'
  ),

  tcga_segments AS (
    SELECT
      sample_id,
      chromosome,
      start_pos AS segment_start,
      end_pos AS segment_end,
      segment_mean,
      CASE
        WHEN segment_mean > 0.8 THEN 'Amplification'
        WHEN segment_mean > 0.2 AND segment_mean <= 0.8 THEN 'Gain'
        WHEN segment_mean < -0.8 THEN 'Deletion'
        WHEN segment_mean < -0.2 AND segment_mean >= -0.8 THEN 'Loss'
        ELSE 'Normal'
      END AS aberration_type
    FROM `isb-cgc.tcga_2019_02.Copy_Number_Segment`
    WHERE project_id = 'TCGA-BRCA'
      AND segment_mean IS NOT NULL
  ),

  tcga_count AS (
    SELECT
      chr.chromosome,
      chr.cytoband_name,
      s.aberration_type,
      COUNT(DISTINCT s.sample_id) AS sample_count
    FROM `mitelman-db.prod.CytoBands_hg38` chr
    INNER JOIN tcga_segments s
      ON s.chromosome = chr.chromosome
         AND s.segment_start < chr.hg38_stop
         AND s.segment_end > chr.hg38_start
    WHERE s.aberration_type IN ('Amplification', 'Gain', 'Loss', 'Deletion')
    GROUP BY chromosome, cytoband_name, aberration_type
  ),

  tcga_freq AS (
    SELECT
      chromosome,
      cytoband_name,
      aberration_type,
      SAFE_DIVIDE(sample_count, (SELECT cnt FROM tcga_total_samples)) * 100 AS freq
    FROM tcga_count
  ),

  -- join Mitelman and TCGA frequencies on chromosome, cytoband, and aberration type
  combined AS (
    SELECT
      m.chromosome,
      m.cytoband_name,
      m.aberration_type,
      m.freq AS mitelman_freq,
      t.freq AS tcga_freq
    FROM mitelman_freq m
    INNER JOIN tcga_freq t
      ON m.chromosome = t.chromosome
         AND m.cytoband_name = t.cytoband_name
         AND m.aberration_type = t.aberration_type
  )

-- final correlation per chromosome and aberration type
SELECT
  chromosome,
  aberration_type,
  ROUND(CORR(mitelman_freq, tcga_freq), 4) AS correlation_coefficient,
  ROUND(`isb-cgc-bq.functions.corr_pvalue_current`(CORR(mitelman_freq, tcga_freq), COUNT(*)), 4) AS p_value
FROM combined
GROUP BY chromosome, aberration_type
HAVING COUNT(*) >= 5
ORDER BY chromosome, aberration_type;
```

<details>
<summary><b>View SlayQL SQL (❌)</b></summary>

```sql
-- This query computes Pearson correlation between Mitelman and TCGA copy number aberration frequencies per chromosome.
-- It uses CytoConverter data for Mitelman and assumes a precomputed TCGA cytoband frequency table.
-- Correlation is computed for four aberration types: amplification, gain, loss, deletion.
-- Only correlations with at least 5 data points (cytobands) are returned.

WITH
-- Step 1: Identify all distinct Mitelman cases with morph=3111 and topo=0401
mitelman_cases AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT RefNo, CaseNo, InvNo
  FROM `mitelman-db.prod.Cytogen`
  WHERE Morph = '3111' AND Topo = '0401'
),

-- Total number of distinct cases in the cohort
total_cases AS (
  SELECT COUNT(*) AS cnt FROM mitelman_cases
),

-- Step 2: For each cytoband, count Mitelman cases with gain or loss overlapping that cytoband
-- Use CytoBands_hg38 for cytoband definitions
mitelman_cytoband_freq AS (
  SELECT
    cb.chromosome,
    cb.cytoband_name,
    COUNT(DISTINCT CONCAT(cc.RefNo, '_', cc.CaseNo, '_', cc.InvNo)) AS gain_cases,
    COUNT(DISTINCT CONCAT(cc_l.RefNo, '_', cc_l.CaseNo, '_', cc_l.InvNo)) AS loss_cases
  FROM `mitelman-db.prod.CytoBands_hg38` AS cb
  LEFT JOIN `mitelman-db.prod.CytoConverted` AS cc
    ON cb.chromosome = cc.Chr
   AND cc.Start < cb.hg38_stop  -- overlap condition
   AND cc.End > cb.hg38_start
   AND cc.Type = 'Gain'
   AND CONCAT(cc.RefNo, '_', cc.CaseNo, '_', cc.InvNo) IN (SELECT CONCAT(RefNo, '_', CaseNo, '_', InvNo) FROM mitelman_cases)
  LEFT JOIN `mitelman-db.prod.CytoConverted` AS cc_l
    ON cb.chromosome = cc_l.Chr
   AND cc_l.Start < cb.hg38_stop
   AND cc_l.End > cb.hg38_start
   AND cc_l.Type = 'Loss'
   AND CONCAT(cc_l.RefNo, '_', cc_l.CaseNo, '_', cc_l.InvNo) IN (SELECT CONCAT(RefNo, '_', CaseNo, '_', InvNo) FROM mitelman_cases)
  GROUP BY cb.chromosome, cb.cytoband_name
),

-- Step 3: Compute frequencies (fraction of cases)
mitelman_freq AS (
  SELECT
    chromosome,
    cytoband_name,
    gain_cases / (SELECT cnt FROM total_cases) AS freq_gain_mitelman,
    loss_cases / (SELECT cnt FROM total_cases) AS freq_loss_mitelman
  FROM mitelman_cytoband_freq
),

-- Step 4: Assumed TCGA precomputed frequencies per cytoband
-- (This CTE is a placeholder – replace with actual TCGA query if needed)
tcga_freq AS (
  SELECT
    chromosome,
    cytoband_name,
    freq_amp,
    freq_gain,
    freq_hetero_del AS freq_hetero_loss,  -- heterozygous deletion
    freq_homo_del AS freq_homo_deletion   -- homozygous deletion
  FROM `isb-cgc-bq.TCGA_version.cytoband_freq`  -- example table, adjust as needed
  WHERE cancer_type = 'BRCA'  -- specify the cancer type (BRCA = breast, matching morph=3111)
),

-- Step 5: Join Mitelman and TCGA frequencies on chromosome and cytoband
combined AS (
  SELECT
    m.chromosome,
    m.cytoband_name,
    m.freq_gain_mitelman,
    m.freq_loss_mitelman,
    t.freq_amp,
    t.freq_gain AS tcga_gain,
    t.freq_hetero_loss AS tcga_hetero_loss,
    t.freq_homo_deletion AS tcga_homo_del
  FROM mitelman_freq AS m
  INNER JOIN tcga_freq AS t
    ON m.chromosome = t.chromosome AND m.cytoband_name = t.cytoband_name
),

-- Step 6: Compute Pearson correlation for each chromosome and aberration type
corr_amp AS (
  SELECT
    chromosome,
    'amplification' AS aberration_type,
    COUNT(*) AS n,
    CORR(freq_gain_mitelman, freq_amp) AS corr
  FROM combined
  WHERE freq_gain_mitelman IS NOT NULL AND freq_amp IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY chromosome
),
corr_gain AS (
  SELECT
    chromosome,
    'gain' AS aberration_type,
    COUNT(*) AS n,
    CORR(freq_gain_mitelman, tcga_gain) AS corr
  FROM combined
  WHERE freq_gain_mitelman IS NOT NULL AND tcga_gain IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY chromosome
),
corr_loss AS (
  SELECT
    chromosome,
    'loss' AS aberration_type,
    COUNT(*) AS n,
    CORR(freq_loss_mitelman, tcga_hetero_loss) AS corr
  FROM combined
  WHERE freq_loss_mitelman IS NOT NULL AND tcga_hetero_loss IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY chromosome
),
corr_del AS (
  SELECT
    chromosome,
    'deletion' AS aberration_type,
    COUNT(*) AS n,
    CORR(freq_loss_mitelman, tcga_homo_del) AS corr
  FROM combined
  WHERE freq_loss_mitelman IS NOT NULL AND tcga_homo_del IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY chromosome
),

-- Union all four aberration types
all_corr AS (
  SELECT * FROM corr_amp
  UNION ALL
  SELECT * FROM corr_gain
  UNION ALL
  SELECT * FROM corr_loss
  UNION ALL
  SELECT * FROM corr_del
)

-- Step 7: Filter by at least 5 data points and compute p-value
SELECT
  chromosome,
  aberration_type,
  ROUND(corr, 4) AS correlation,
  ROUND(isb_cgc_bq.functions.corr_pvalue_current(corr, n), 6) AS p_value
FROM all_corr
WHERE n >= 5 AND corr IS NOT NULL
ORDER BY chromosome, aberration_type;
```
</details>

#### 📜 Generated SQL Queries

<details>
<summary><b>View Baseline SQL (❌)</b></summary>

```sql
-- Step 1: Filter variants on chromosome 12 and flatten the call array
WITH variant_calls AS (
    SELECT 
        V."start",
        V."end",
        V."call" AS call_data
    FROM "_1000_GENOMES"."_1000_GENOMES"."VARIANTS" V
    WHERE V."reference_name" = '12'
),

-- Step 2: Unnest the call array to get individual sample genotypes
flattened_calls AS (
    SELECT
        VC."start",
        VC."end",
        f.value:"call_set_name"::STRING AS sample_id,
        f.value:"genotype"::ARRAY AS genotype_array
    FROM variant_calls VC,
    LATERAL FLATTEN(input => VC.call_data) f
),

-- Step 3: Unnest the genotype array to get individual alleles (0 or 1)
alleles AS (
    SELECT
        FC."start",
        FC."end",
        FC.sample_id,
        g.value::INTEGER AS allele
    FROM flattened_calls FC,
    LATERAL FLATTEN(input => FC.genotype_array) g
),

-- Step 4: Join with SAMPLE_INFO to get super population
allele_with_pop AS (
    SELECT
        a."start",
        a."end",
        a.allele,
        CASE WHEN si."Super_Population" = 'EAS' THEN 'case' ELSE 'control' END AS group_type
    FROM alleles a
    JOIN "_1000_GENOMES"."_1000_GENOMES"."SAMPLE_INFO" si 
      ON a.sample_id = si."Sample"
),

-- Step 5: Aggregate per variant: counts for each cell in 2x2 table
counts AS (
    SELECT
        "start",
        "end",
        SUM(CASE WHEN group_type = 'case' AND allele = 0 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS case_ref,
        SUM(CASE WHEN group_type = 'case' AND allele = 1 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS case_alt,
        SUM(CASE WHEN group_type = 'control' AND allele = 0 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS control_ref,
        SUM(CASE WHEN group_type = 'control' AND allele = 1 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS control_alt
    FROM allele_with_pop
    GROUP BY "start", "end"
),

-- Step 6: Compute row, column totals and expected values
expected_values AS (
    SELECT
        c.*,
        (c.case_ref + c.case_alt)::FLOAT AS case_total,
        (c.control_ref + c.control_alt)::FLOAT AS control_total,
        (c.case_ref + c.control_ref)::FLOAT AS ref_total,
        (c.case_alt + c.control_alt)::FLOAT AS alt_total,
        (c.case_ref + c.case_alt + c.control_ref + c.control_alt)::FLOAT AS grand_total
    FROM counts c
    WHERE (c.case_ref + c.case_alt + c.control_ref + c.control_alt) > 0
),

-- Step 7: Filter variants where all expected counts >= 5
valid_variants AS (
    SELECT
        e.*,
        (e.case_total * e.ref_total) / NULLIF(e.grand_total, 0) AS exp_case_ref,
        (e.case_total * e.alt_total) / NULLIF(e.grand_total, 0) AS exp_case_alt,
        (e.control_total * e.ref_total) / NULLIF(e.grand_total, 0) AS exp_control_ref,
        (e.control_total * e.alt_total) / NULLIF(e.grand_total, 0) AS exp_control_alt
    FROM expected_values e
    WHERE (e.case_total * e.ref_total) / NULLIF(e.grand_total, 0) >= 5
      AND (e.case_total * e.alt_total) / NULLIF(e.grand_total, 0) >= 5
      AND (e.control_total * e.ref_total) / NULLIF(e.grand_total, 0) >= 5
      AND (e.control_total * e.alt_total) / NULLIF(e.grand_total, 0) >= 5
),

-- Step 8: Compute chi-squared with Yates's correction
chi_sq AS (
    SELECT
        "start",
        "end",
        ROUND(
            CASE WHEN ABS(case_ref - exp_case_ref) > 0.5
                 THEN POWER(ABS(case_ref - exp_case_ref) - 0.5, 2) / NULLIF(exp_case_ref, 0)
                 ELSE 0 END +
            CASE WHEN ABS(case_alt - exp_case_alt) > 0.5
                 THEN POWER(ABS(case_alt - exp_case_alt) - 0.5, 2) / NULLIF(exp_case_alt, 0)
                 ELSE 0 END +
            CASE WHEN ABS(control_ref - exp_control_ref) > 0.5
                 THEN POWER(ABS(control_ref - exp_control_ref) - 0.5, 2) / NULLIF(exp_control_ref, 0)
                 ELSE 0 END +
            CASE WHEN ABS(control_alt - exp_control_alt) > 0.5
                 THEN POWER(ABS(control_alt - exp_control_alt) - 0.5, 2) / NULLIF(exp_control_alt, 0)
                 ELSE 0 END,
            4
        ) AS chi_squared
    FROM valid_variants
)

-- Step 9: Return top variants with chi_squared >= threshold
SELECT "start", "end", chi_squared
FROM chi_sq
WHERE chi_squared >= 29.71679
ORDER BY chi_squared DESC;
```

<summary><b>View SlayQL SQL (❌)</b></summary>

```sql
WITH
-- Step 1: Flatten call array to extract per-individual allele counts for variants on chr12
per_variant_ind AS (
  SELECT
    v."start",
    v."end",
    v."reference_name",
    f.value:"call_set_name"::STRING AS "individual_id",
    (f.value:"genotype"[0]::INT + f.value:"genotype"[1]::INT) AS "alt_allele_count"
  FROM "_1000_GENOMES"."_1000_GENOMES"."VARIANTS" v,
  LATERAL FLATTEN(input => v."call") f
  WHERE v."reference_name" = '12'
),

-- Step 2: Join with sample info to get super population
ind_info AS (
  SELECT
    p."individual_id",
    p."alt_allele_count",
    p."start",
    p."end",
    s."Super_Population"
  FROM per_variant_ind p
  JOIN "_1000_GENOMES"."_1000_GENOMES"."SAMPLE_INFO" s
    ON p."individual_id" = s."Sample"
),

-- Step 3: Aggregate allele counts for cases (EAS) and controls (all others)
grouped AS (
  SELECT
    "start",
    "end",
    SUM(CASE WHEN "Super_Population" = 'EAS' THEN "alt_allele_count" ELSE 0 END) AS "alt_cases",
    SUM(CASE WHEN "Super_Population" != 'EAS' THEN "alt_allele_count" ELSE 0 END) AS "alt_controls",
    COUNT(CASE WHEN "Super_Population" = 'EAS' THEN 1 END) * 2 AS "total_cases_alleles",
    COUNT(CASE WHEN "Super_Population" != 'EAS' THEN 1 END) * 2 AS "total_controls_alleles"
  FROM ind_info
  GROUP BY "start", "end"
)

-- Step 4: Compute chi-squared with Yates correction and filter
SELECT
  "start",
  "end",
  ROUND(
    -- Yates chi-squared = (|ad - bc| - N/2)^2 * N / ( (a+b)(c+d)(a+c)(b+d) )
    (
      POW(
        ABS(
          "alt_cases" * ("total_controls_alleles" - "alt_controls")
          - "alt_controls" * ("total_cases_alleles" - "alt_cases")
        ) - ("total_cases_alleles" + "total_controls_alleles") / 2.0,
        2
      ) * ("total_cases_alleles" + "total_controls_alleles")
    ) / (
      ("alt_cases" + "alt_controls")
      * (("total_cases_alleles" + "total_controls_alleles") - ("alt_cases" + "alt_controls"))
      * "total_cases_alleles"
      * "total_controls_alleles"
    ),
    4
  ) AS "chi_squared"
FROM grouped
WHERE
  -- Ensure all expected cell counts are >= 5
  ("alt_cases" + "alt_controls") * "total_cases_alleles" / ("total_cases_alleles" + "total_controls_alleles") >= 5
  AND ("alt_cases" + "alt_controls") * "total_controls_alleles" / ("total_cases_alleles" + "total_controls_alleles") >= 5
  AND (("total_cases_alleles" + "total_controls_alleles") - ("alt_cases" + "alt_controls")) * "total_cases_alleles" / ("total_cases_alleles" + "total_controls_alleles") >= 5
  AND (("total_cases_alleles" + "total_controls_alleles") - ("alt_cases" + "alt_controls")) * "total_controls_alleles" / ("total_cases_alleles" + "total_controls_alleles") >= 5
  AND ROUND(
    (
      POW(
        ABS(
          "alt_cases" * ("total_controls_alleles" - "alt_controls")
          - "alt_controls" * ("total_cases_alleles" - "alt_cases")
        ) - ("total_cases_alleles" + "total_controls_alleles") / 2.0,
        2
      ) * ("total_cases_alleles" + "total_controls_alleles")
    ) / (
      ("alt_cases" + "alt_controls")
      * (("total_cases_alleles" + "total_controls_alleles") - ("alt_cases" + "alt_controls"))
      * "total_cases_alleles"
      * "total_controls_alleles"
    ),
    4
  ) >= 29.71679
ORDER BY "chi_squared" DESC;
```

```sql
-- Count distinct bike share stations per year (2013 and 2014) and per status (active/closed)
-- Using the 'bikeshare_stations' table's modified_date to determine the year
WITH station_status_per_year AS (
  SELECT
    station_id,
    status,
    EXTRACT(YEAR FROM modified_date) AS station_year
  FROM
    `bigquery-public-data.austin_bikeshare.bikeshare_stations`
  WHERE
    status IN ('active', 'closed')
    AND EXTRACT(YEAR FROM modified_date) IN (2013, 2014)
)
SELECT
  station_year AS year,
  status,
  COUNT(DISTINCT station_id) AS number_of_distinct_stations
FROM
  station_status_per_year
GROUP BY
  year, status
ORDER BY
  year, status;
```

```sql
WITH 
-- Step 1: Identify currently active stations (status = 'active')
"active_stations" AS (
    SELECT "station_id"
    FROM "AUSTIN"."AUSTIN_BIKESHARE"."BIKESHARE_STATIONS"
    WHERE "status" = 'active'
),
-- Step 2: For each active station, compute total starting trips and average duration
"trips_summary" AS (
    SELECT 
        t."start_station_id" AS "station_id",
        COUNT(t."trip_id") AS "total_trips",

    FROM "AUSTIN"."AUSTIN_BIKESHARE"."BIKESHARE_TRIPS" t
    INNER JOIN "active_stations" a ON t."start_station_id" = a."station_id"
    GROUP BY t."start_station_id"
),
-- Step 3: Compute the overall total trips from active stations (needed for percentage)
"overall_total" AS (
    SELECT SUM("total_trips") AS "overall_trips"
    FROM "trips_summary"
),
-- Step 4: Rank stations by total trips descending (using RANK to include ties)
"ranked" AS (
    SELECT 
        s."station_id",
        s."total_trips",
        s."avg_duration",
        o."overall_trips",
        RANK() OVER (ORDER BY s."total_trips" DESC) AS "rank"
    FROM "trips_summary" s
    CROSS JOIN "overall_total" o
)
-- Step 5: Select top 15 (including ties) and compute percentage
SELECT 
    "station_id",
    "total_trips",
    ROUND(("total_trips" / "overall_trips") * 100, 4) AS "percentage",
    ROUND("avg_duration", 4) AS "avg_duration_minutes"
FROM "ranked"
WHERE "rank" <= 15
ORDER BY "rank";
```

```sql
WITH
-- Step 1: Join active stations with their starting trips
active_station_trips AS (
    SELECT 
        s."station_id",
        t."duration_minutes"
    FROM "AUSTIN"."AUSTIN_BIKESHARE"."BIKESHARE_STATIONS" s
    INNER JOIN "AUSTIN"."AUSTIN_BIKESHARE"."BIKESHARE_TRIPS" t
        ON s."station_id" = t."start_station_id"
    WHERE LOWER(s."status") = 'active'
),

-- Step 2: Aggregate per station: total trips and avg duration
station_stats AS (
    SELECT 
        "station_id",
        COUNT(*) AS "total_trips",
        ROUND(AVG("duration_minutes"), 4) AS "avg_duration_minutes"
    FROM active_station_trips
    GROUP BY "station_id"
),

-- Step 3: Compute the grand total of trips from all active stations
overall_total AS (
    SELECT SUM("total_trips") AS "grand_total"
    FROM station_stats
),

-- Step 4: Rank stations by total trips (DENSE_RANK includes ties)
ranked_stations AS (
    SELECT 
        "station_id",
        "total_trips",
        "avg_duration_minutes",
        DENSE_RANK() OVER (ORDER BY "total_trips" DESC) AS "rank"
    FROM station_stats
)

-- Step 5: Final selection of top 15 stations (including ties)
SELECT 
    "station_id",
    "total_trips",
    ROUND("total_trips" * 100.0 / (SELECT "grand_total" FROM overall_total), 4) AS "percentage",
    "avg_duration_minutes"
FROM ranked_stations
WHERE "rank" <= 15
ORDER BY "rank";
```

#### 📜 Generated SQL Queries

<details>
<summary><b>View Baseline SQL (❌)</b></summary>

```sql
-- Step 1: Filter activities based on molecule properties, pChEMBL, standard value, and duplicate limits
WITH filtered_activities AS (
    SELECT 
        a.assay_id,
        a.doc_id,
        a.molregno,
        a.standard_type,
        a.standard_value,
        a.standard_relation,
        a.activity_id,
        a.pchembl_value,
        a.potential_duplicate,
        cp.heavy_atoms,
        cs.canonical_smiles
    FROM `bigquery-public-data.ebi_chembl.activities` a
    JOIN `bigquery-public-data.ebi_chembl.compound_properties` cp 
        ON a.molregno = cp.molregno
    JOIN `bigquery-public-data.ebi_chembl.compound_structures` cs 
        ON a.molregno = cs.molregno
    WHERE 
        -- heavy atoms between 10 and 15
        SAFE_CAST(cp.heavy_atoms AS INT64) BETWEEN 10 AND 15
        -- pChEMBL > 10 and not null
        AND a.pchembl_value IS NOT NULL 
        AND SAFE_CAST(a.pchembl_value AS FLOAT64) > 10
        -- standard_value not null
        AND a.standard_value IS NOT NULL
),

-- Step 2: Aggregate per molecule, assay, standard type
activity_stats AS (
    SELECT 
        assay_id,
        standard_type,
        molregno,
        COUNT(*) AS activity_count,
        SUM(SAFE_CAST(potential_duplicate AS INT64)) AS dup_count,
        -- Pick the activity with the highest activity_id as representative
        ARRAY_AGG(activity_id ORDER BY activity_id DESC LIMIT 1)[OFFSET(0)] AS rep_activity_id,
        ARRAY_AGG(doc_id ORDER BY activity_id DESC LIMIT 1)[OFFSET(0)] AS rep_doc_id,
        ARRAY_AGG(standard_value ORDER BY activity_id DESC LIMIT 1)[OFFSET(0)] AS rep_std_value,
        ARRAY_AGG(standard_relation ORDER BY activity_id DESC LIMIT 1)[OFFSET(0)] AS rep_std_relation,
        ARRAY_AGG(canonical_smiles ORDER BY activity_id DESC LIMIT 1)[OFFSET(0)] AS canonical_smiles,
        ANY_VALUE(heavy_atoms) AS heavy_atoms   -- same for all rows of the molecule
    FROM filtered_activities
    GROUP BY assay_id, standard_type, molregno
    HAVING 
        activity_count < 5 
        AND dup_count < 2
),

-- Step 3: Self-join to find pairs (different molecules, same assay and standard type)
pairs AS (
    SELECT 
        a.assay_id,
        a.standard_type,
        a.molregno AS molregno1,
        b.molregno AS molregno2,
        a.rep_activity_id AS act_id1,
        b.rep_activity_id AS act_id2,
        a.rep_doc_id AS doc_id1,
        b.rep_doc_id AS doc_id2,
        a.rep_std_value AS std_val1,
        b.rep_std_value AS std_val2,
        a.rep_std_relation AS std_rel1,
        b.rep_std_relation AS std_rel2,
        a.canonical_smiles AS smi1,
        b.canonical_smiles AS smi2,
        GREATEST(SAFE_CAST(a.heavy_atoms AS INT64), SAFE_CAST(b.heavy_atoms AS INT64)) AS max_heavy_atoms
    FROM activity_stats a
    JOIN activity_stats b 
        ON a.assay_id = b.assay_id 
        AND a.standard_type = b.standard_type 
        AND a.molregno < b.molregno
),

-- Step 4: Compute percent rank for all documents (needed for date calculation)
doc_rank AS (
    SELECT 
        doc_id,
        journal,
        year,
        first_page,
        ROW_NUMBER() OVER (
            PARTITION BY journal, year 
            ORDER BY SAFE_CAST(first_page AS INT64) ASC
        ) AS rn,
        COUNT(*) OVER (PARTITION BY journal, year) AS cnt
    FROM `bigquery-public-data.ebi_chembl.docs`
    WHERE 
        year IS NOT NULL 
        AND first_page IS NOT NULL 
        AND journal IS NOT NULL
        AND SAFE_CAST(year AS INT64) IS NOT NULL
        AND SAFE_CAST(first_page AS INT64) IS NOT NULL
),

doc_date AS (
    SELECT 
        doc_id,
        SAFE_CAST(year AS INT64) AS pub_year,
        CASE 
            WHEN cnt = 1 THEN 0.0 
            ELSE (rn - 1.0) / (cnt - 1.0) 
        END AS percent_rank
    FROM doc_rank
),

doc_final_date AS (
    SELECT 
        doc_id,
        pub_year,
        FLOOR(percent_rank * 11) + 1 AS pub_month,
        (FLOOR(percent_rank * 308) % 28) + 1 AS pub_day
    FROM doc_date
),

-- Step 5: Combine pairs with document dates and compute final outputs
pair_dates AS (
    SELECT 
        p.*,
        d1.pub_year AS pub_year1,
        d1.pub_month AS pub_month1,
        d1.pub_day AS pub_day1,
        d2.pub_year AS pub_year2,
        d2.pub_month AS pub_month2,
        d2.pub_day AS pub_day2,
        -- Highest document id among the two
        GREATEST(SAFE_CAST(p.doc_id1 AS INT64), SAFE_CAST(p.doc_id2 AS INT64)) AS highest_doc_id,
        -- Latest publication date as DATE
        GREATEST(
            DATE(d1.pub_year, d1.pub_month, d1.pub_day),
            DATE(d2.pub_year, d2.pub_month, d2.pub_day)
        ) AS latest_pub_date
    FROM pairs p
    LEFT JOIN doc_final_date d1 ON p.doc_id1 = d1.doc_id
    LEFT JOIN doc_final_date d2 ON p.doc_id2 = d2.doc_id
),

final AS (
    SELECT 
        max_heavy_atoms,
        FORMAT_DATE('%Y-%m-%d', latest_pub_date) AS latest_publication_date,
        highest_doc_id,
        -- Classify change in standard values
        CASE
            WHEN SAFE_CAST(std_val1 AS FLOAT64) > SAFE_CAST(std_val2 AS FLOAT64) 
                 AND std_rel1 NOT IN ('<', '<=')
                 AND std_rel2 NOT IN ('>', '>=') 
            THEN 'decrease'
            WHEN SAFE_CAST(std_val1 AS FLOAT64) < SAFE_CAST(std_val2 AS FLOAT64) 
                 AND std_rel1 NOT IN ('>', '>=')
                 AND std_rel2 NOT IN ('<', '<=') 
            THEN 'increase'
            WHEN SAFE_CAST(std_val1 AS FLOAT64) = SAFE_CAST(std_val2 AS FLOAT64) 
                 AND std_rel1 = '=' 
                 AND std_rel2 = '=' 
            THEN 'no-change'
            ELSE 'unknown'
        END AS std_change,
        -- UUID from activity IDs
        TO_HEX(MD5(TO_JSON_STRING(STRUCT(act_id1, act_id2)))) AS uuid_activity_ids,
        -- UUID from canonical SMILES
        TO_HEX(MD5(TO_JSON_STRING(STRUCT(smi1, smi2)))) AS uuid_canonical_smiles
    FROM pair_dates
)

-- Final output
SELECT * FROM final;
```
</details>

```sql
-- Use tables from ChEMBL release 29 (based on external knowledge)
WITH 
-- Compute synthetic publication date for each document
docs_with_date AS (
  SELECT 
    doc_id,
    journal,
    year,
    first_page,
    -- Year: use publication year, default 1970 if missing
    COALESCE(SAFE_CAST(year AS INT64), 1970) AS pub_year,
    -- Percent rank within same journal and year, ordered by first page numeric value
    PERCENT_RANK() OVER (
      PARTITION BY journal, year 
      ORDER BY SAFE_CAST(first_page AS INT64)
    ) AS pct_rank
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.ebi_chembl.docs_29`
  WHERE journal IS NOT NULL AND year IS NOT NULL AND first_page IS NOT NULL
),
-- Compute month and day from percent rank, then construct date
doc_date AS (
  SELECT 
    doc_id,
    pub_year,
    -- Month: floor(pct_rank * 11) + 1
    FLOOR(pct_rank * 11) + 1 AS pub_month,
    -- Day: (floor(pct_rank * 308) % 28) + 1
    MOD(FLOOR(pct_rank * 308), 28) + 1 AS pub_day
  FROM docs_with_date
),
-- Prepare filtered activities with all required conditions
filtered_activities AS (
  SELECT 
    a.activity_id,
    a.assay_id,
    a.standard_type,
    a.molregno,
    a.doc_id,
    a.standard_value,
    a.standard_relation,
    a.pchembl_value,
    -- Heavy atoms (cast to int)
    SAFE_CAST(cp.heavy_atoms AS INT64) AS heavy_atoms,
    -- Canonical SMILES
    cs.canonical_smiles,
    -- Document date
    dd.pub_year,
    dd.pub_month,
    dd.pub_day,
    -- Synthetic date as DATE
    DATE(dd.pub_year, dd.pub_month, dd.pub_day) AS pub_date,
    -- Count activities per (molregno, assay) and duplicate count
    COUNT(*) OVER (PARTITION BY a.molregno, a.assay_id) AS activity_count,
    COUNTIF(a.potential_duplicate = '1') OVER (PARTITION BY a.molregno, a.assay_id) AS duplicate_count
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.ebi_chembl.activities_29` a
  JOIN `bigquery-public-data.ebi_chembl.compound_properties_29` cp
    ON a.molregno = cp.molregno
  JOIN `bigquery-public-data.ebi_chembl.compound_structures_29` cs
    ON a.molregno = cs.molregno
  JOIN doc_date dd
    ON a.doc_id = dd.doc_id
  WHERE 
    -- Non-null standard value
    a.standard_value IS NOT NULL
    -- pChEMBL > 10
    AND SAFE_CAST(a.pchembl_value AS FLOAT64) > 10
    -- Heavy atoms between 10 and 15 inclusive
    AND SAFE_CAST(cp.heavy_atoms AS INT64) BETWEEN 10 AND 15
    -- Standard relation must be '=' for unambiguous comparison
    AND a.standard_relation = '='
)
-- Now find pairs of different molecules in same assay and standard type
SELECT 
  -- Maximum heavy atom count (as integer)
  GREATEST(a.heavy_atoms, b.heavy_atoms) AS max_heavy_atom_count,
  -- Latest publication date
  GREATEST(a.pub_date, b.pub_date) AS latest_publication_date,
  -- Highest document ID
  GREATEST(a.doc_id, b.doc_id) AS highest_doc_id,
  -- Classify change in standard values
  CASE
    WHEN SAFE_CAST(a.standard_value AS FLOAT64) > SAFE_CAST(b.standard_value AS FLOAT64) THEN 'decrease'
    WHEN SAFE_CAST(a.standard_value AS FLOAT64) < SAFE_CAST(b.standard_value AS FLOAT64) THEN 'increase'
    ELSE 'no-change'
  END AS change_classification,
  -- UUID generated from both activity IDs and both canonical SMILES
  TO_HEX(
    MD5(
      TO_JSON_STRING(
        STRUCT(a.activity_id AS a1, b.activity_id AS a2, a.canonical_smiles AS s1, b.canonical_smiles AS s2)
      )
    )
  ) AS pair_uuid
FROM filtered_activities a
JOIN filtered_activities b
  ON a.assay_id = b.assay_id
    AND a.standard_type = b.standard_type
    AND a.molregno < b.molregno
WHERE 
  -- Both molecules must satisfy the activity count conditions
  a.activity_count < 5
  AND b.activity_count < 5
  AND a.duplicate_count < 2
  AND b.duplicate_count < 2;
```
</details>

#### 📜 Generated SQL Queries

<details>
<summary><b>View Baseline SQL (❌)</b></summary>

```sql
-- This query retrieves 2016 committees that supported at least one candidate and
-- received individual small-dollar contributions (amount > 0 and < 200) totalling more than $0.
-- For each committee: name, number of unique candidates supported, alphabetical candidate names,
-- and total sum of small-dollar contributions.

WITH
  -- Committees that are linked to at least one candidate in 2016
  committees_with_candidates AS (
    SELECT DISTINCT
      c.cmte_id,
      c.cmte_nm,
      l.cand_id
    FROM `bigquery-public-data.fec.committee_2016` c
    INNER JOIN `bigquery-public-data.fec.candidate_committee_2016` l
      ON c.cmte_id = l.cmte_id
      AND l.fec_election_yr = 2016
  ),

  -- Candidate names for each candidate ID
  candidate_names AS (
    SELECT cand_id, cand_name
    FROM `bigquery-public-data.fec.candidate_2016`
  ),

  -- Individual contributions to 2016 committees that are small-dollar (0 < amount < 200)
  small_dollar_contributions AS (
    SELECT
      cmte_id,
      transaction_amt
    FROM `bigquery-public-data.fec.committee_contributions_2016`
    WHERE transaction_amt > 0
      AND transaction_amt < 200
  ),

  -- Aggregate small-dollar contributions per committee
  committee_small_dollar AS (
    SELECT
      cmte_id,
      SUM(transaction_amt) AS total_small_dollar
    FROM small_dollar_contributions
    GROUP BY cmte_id
    HAVING SUM(transaction_amt) > 0
  ),

  -- Combine candidate information per committee (distinct candidates)
  committee_candidates AS (
    SELECT
      cwc.cmte_id,
      cwc.cmte_nm,
      cn.cand_name
    FROM committees_with_candidates cwc
    INNER JOIN candidate_names cn
      ON cwc.cand_id = cn.cand_id
  ),

  -- Aggregate candidate count and sorted names per committee
  committee_candidate_agg AS (
    SELECT
      cmte_id,
      cmte_nm,
      COUNT(DISTINCT cand_name) AS num_candidates,
      STRING_AGG(DISTINCT cand_name, ',' ORDER BY cand_name) AS candidate_names
    FROM committee_candidates
    GROUP BY cmte_id, cmte_nm
  )

-- Final result: committees with both candidate support and small-dollar contributions
SELECT
  cca.cmte_nm AS committee_name,
  cca.num_candidates,
  cca.candidate_names,
  csd.total_small_dollar
FROM committee_candidate_agg cca
INNER JOIN committee_small_dollar csd
  ON cca.cmte_id = csd.cmte_id
ORDER BY committee_name;
```
</details>

<details>
<summary><b>View SlayQL SQL (❌)</b></summary>

```sql
WITH small_dollar_committees AS (
    -- Find committees with individual contributions > $0 and < $200, summing to > $0
    SELECT 
        cmte_id,
        SUM(transaction_amt) AS total_small_dollar
    FROM `bigquery-public-data.fec.committee_contributions_2016`
    WHERE transaction_amt > 0 AND transaction_amt < 200
    GROUP BY cmte_id
    HAVING SUM(transaction_amt) > 0
),
committee_candidate_links AS (
    -- Get committees that supported at least one candidate in the 2016 election cycle
    SELECT DISTINCT
        cc.cmte_id,
        cc.cand_id
    FROM `bigquery-public-data.fec.candidate_committee_2016` cc
    WHERE cc.fec_election_yr = 2016
),
qualifying_committees AS (
    -- Committees that have small-dollar contributions AND support at least one candidate
    SELECT 
        sdc.cmte_id,
        sdc.total_small_dollar
    FROM small_dollar_committees sdc
    WHERE EXISTS (
        SELECT 1 
        FROM committee_candidate_links ccl 
        WHERE ccl.cmte_id = sdc.cmte_id
    )
),
committee_candidates AS (
    -- Resolve committee names and linked candidate names for qualifying committees
    SELECT 
        qc.cmte_id,
        c.cmte_nm,
        qc.total_small_dollar,
        cand.cand_id,
        cand.cand_name
    FROM qualifying_committees qc
    JOIN `bigquery-public-data.fec.committee_2016` c ON qc.cmte_id = c.cmte_id
    JOIN `bigquery-public-data.fec.candidate_committee_2016` cc ON qc.cmte_id = cc.cmte_id
    JOIN `bigquery-public-data.fec.candidate_2016` cand ON cc.cand_id = cand.cand_id
    WHERE cc.fec_election_yr = 2016
)
-- Final aggregation: one row per committee with candidate list, count, and total
SELECT 
    cmte_nm AS committee_name,
    COUNT(DISTINCT cand_id) AS unique_candidates_count,
    STRING_AGG(cand_name, ', ' ORDER BY cand_name) AS candidates_names,
    total_small_dollar
FROM committee_candidates
GROUP BY cmte_id, cmte_nm, total_small_dollar
ORDER BY cmte_nm;
```
</details>

#### 📜 Generated SQL Queries

<details>
<summary><b>View Baseline SQL (❌)</b></summary>

```sql
-- Step 1: Filter records within the date range
WITH filtered AS (
  SELECT *
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.fda_food.food_events`
  WHERE date_created BETWEEN DATE '2015-01-01' AND DATE '2015-01-31'
    AND date_started BETWEEN DATE '2015-01-01' AND DATE '2015-01-31'
),

-- Step 2: Apply data cleansing transformations
cleaned AS (
  SELECT
    *,
    -- Split reactions and outcomes into arrays
    SPLIT(COALESCE(reactions, ''), ', ') AS reactions_array,
    SPLIT(COALESCE(outcomes, ''), ', ') AS outcomes_array,
    -- products_brand_name: preserve numeric patterns (digit,comma,digit) then replace other ", " with " -- "
    REGEXP_REPLACE(
      REGEXP_REPLACE(
        REGEXP_REPLACE(COALESCE(products_brand_name, ''), r'(\d),(\d)', r'\1~~COMMA~~\2'),
        r', ', ' -- '),
      r'~~COMMA~~', ','
    ) AS products_brand_name_cleaned,
    -- Simple replacement for other fields
    REPLACE(COALESCE(products_industry_code, ''), ', ', ' -- ') AS products_industry_code_cleaned,
    REPLACE(COALESCE(products_role, ''), ', ', ' -- ') AS products_role_cleaned,
    REPLACE(COALESCE(products_industry_name, ''), ', ', ' -- ') AS products_industry_name_cleaned
  FROM filtered
)

-- Step 3: Compute array lengths
SELECT
  *,
  -- industry_code_length: treat empty string as 0, else split and count
  CASE
    WHEN TRIM(COALESCE(products_industry_code_cleaned, '')) = '' THEN 0
    ELSE ARRAY_LENGTH(SPLIT(products_industry_code_cleaned, ' -- '))
  END AS industry_code_length,
  -- brand_name_length: similar
  CASE
    WHEN TRIM(COALESCE(products_brand_name_cleaned, '')) = '' THEN 0
    ELSE ARRAY_LENGTH(SPLIT(products_brand_name_cleaned, ' -- '))
  END AS brand_name_length
FROM cleaned;
```
</details>

<details>
<summary><b>View SlayQL SQL (❌)</b></summary>

```sql
WITH
  -- Step 1: Filter rows by date range
  filtered_events AS (
    SELECT
      report_number,
      reactions,
      outcomes,
      date_created,
      date_started,
      consumer_gender,
      consumer_age,
      consumer_age_unit,
      products_brand_name,
      products_industry_code,
      products_role,
      products_industry_name
    FROM `bigquery-public-data.fda_food.food_events`
    WHERE date_created BETWEEN '2015-01-01' AND '2015-01-31'
      AND date_started BETWEEN '2015-01-01' AND '2015-01-31'
  ),

  -- Step 2: Apply all data cleansing transformations
  transformed_events AS (
    SELECT
      report_number,
      -- Split reactions into array by comma-space
      SPLIT(reactions, ', ') AS reactions,
      -- Split outcomes into array by comma-space
      SPLIT(outcomes, ', ') AS outcomes,
      date_created,
      date_started,
      consumer_gender,
      consumer_age,
      consumer_age_unit,
      -- products_brand_name: replace ", " with " -- " except when part of a digit-digit numeric pattern
      REGEXP_REPLACE(products_brand_name, r'(?<!\d), (?!\d)', ' -- ') AS products_brand_name,
      -- products_industry_code: replace ", " with " -- "
      REPLACE(products_industry_code, ', ', ' -- ') AS products_industry_code,
      -- products_role: replace ", " with " -- "
      REPLACE(products_role, ', ', ' -- ') AS products_role,
      -- products_industry_name: replace ", " with " -- "
      REPLACE(products_industry_name, ', ', ' -- ') AS products_industry_name,
      -- Calculate industry_code_length = array length after splitting by " -- "
      ARRAY_LENGTH(
        SPLIT(REPLACE(products_industry_code, ', ', ' -- '), ' -- ')
      ) AS industry_code_length,
      -- Calculate brand_name_length = array length after splitting by " -- "
      ARRAY_LENGTH(
        SPLIT(
          REGEXP_REPLACE(products_brand_name, r'(?<!\d), (?!\d)', ' -- '),
          ' -- '
        )
      ) AS brand_name_length
    FROM filtered_events
  )

-- Final output: the cleansed food events data
SELECT *
FROM transformed_events
ORDER BY report_number;
```
</details>

### 102. sf_bq423 (DB: `GOOGLE_ADS`)
**Question**: Between January 1, 2023, and January 1, 2024, which image-type advertisement on the topic of Health, published by a verified advertiser located in Cyprus, was shown in Croatia, has times_shown_availability_date as NULL (meaning the times shown data is available), utilized demographic information, geo-location targeting, contextual signals, customer lists, and topics of interest without any of these selection methods being unused, and additionally had its first shown date strictly after January 1, 2023, and last shown date strictly before January 1, 2024? Among such ads, provide the page URL of the one with the highest upper bound of times shown.

**Status**: Baseline ❌ | SlayQL ❌

#### 📊 Execution Results Comparison

#### 📜 Generated SQL Queries

<details>
<summary><b>View Baseline SQL (❌)</b></summary>

```sql
WITH 
-- Step 1: Filter ads based on core criteria
filtered_ads AS (
    SELECT 
        cs."creative_page_url",
        cs."region_stats",
        cs."audience_selection_approach_info"
    FROM "GOOGLE_ADS"."GOOGLE_ADS_TRANSPARENCY_CENTER"."CREATIVE_STATS" cs
    WHERE 
        cs."ad_format_type" = 'IMAGE'
        AND cs."topic" = 'Health'
        AND cs."advertiser_verification_status" = 'VERIFIED'
        AND cs."advertiser_location" = 'CY'
        -- All five audience selection methods must be used (not 'CRITERIA_UNUSED')
        AND cs."audience_selection_approach_info":"demographic_info"::STRING != 'CRITERIA_UNUSED'
        AND cs."audience_selection_approach_info":"geo_location"::STRING != 'CRITERIA_UNUSED'
        AND cs."audience_selection_approach_info":"contextual_signals"::STRING != 'CRITERIA_UNUSED'
        AND cs."audience_selection_approach_info":"customer_lists"::STRING != 'CRITERIA_UNUSED'
        AND cs."audience_selection_approach_info":"topics_of_interest"::STRING != 'CRITERIA_UNUSED'
),
-- Step 2: Unnest region_stats and restrict to Croatia (HR)
croatia_region AS (
    SELECT 
        fa."creative_page_url",
        reg.value:"first_shown"::DATE AS "first_shown",
        reg.value:"last_shown"::DATE AS "last_shown",
        reg.value:"times_shown_availability_date"::DATE AS "times_shown_availability_date",
        reg.value:"times_shown_upper_bound"::NUMBER AS "times_shown_upper_bound"
    FROM filtered_ads fa,
         LATERAL FLATTEN(input => fa."region_stats") reg
    WHERE reg.value:"region_code"::STRING = 'HR'
)
-- Step 3: Apply remaining filters, sort by upper bound descending, and pick top URL
SELECT 
    cr."creative_page_url"
FROM croatia_region cr
WHERE 
    cr."times_shown_availability_date" IS NULL          -- times shown data is available
    AND cr."first_shown" > '2023-01-01'                 -- strictly after Jan 1, 2023
    AND cr."last_shown" < '2024-01-01'                  -- strictly before Jan 1, 2024
ORDER BY cr."times_shown_upper_bound" DESC NULLS LAST
LIMIT 1;
```
</details>

<details>
<summary><b>View SlayQL SQL (❌)</b></summary>

```sql
WITH "flattened" AS (
    SELECT 
        cs."creative_page_url",
        cs."ad_format_type",
        cs."topic",
        cs."advertiser_verification_status",
        cs."advertiser_location",
        cs."audience_selection_approach_info",
        r.value AS "region_entry"
    FROM GOOGLE_ADS.GOOGLE_ADS_TRANSPARENCY_CENTER.CREATIVE_STATS cs,
    LATERAL FLATTEN(input => cs."region_stats") r
)
SELECT 
    f."creative_page_url"
FROM "flattened" f
WHERE f."ad_format_type" = 'IMAGE'
  AND f."topic" = 'Health'
  AND f."advertiser_verification_status" = 'VERIFIED'
  AND f."advertiser_location" = 'CY'
  AND f."region_entry":"region_code"::TEXT = 'HR'
  AND f."region_entry":"times_shown_availability_date" IS NULL
  AND f."region_entry":"first_shown"::DATE > '2023-01-01'
  AND f."region_entry":"last_shown"::DATE < '2024-01-01'
  AND f."audience_selection_approach_info":"demographic_info"::TEXT != 'CRITERIA_UNUSED'
  AND f."audience_selection_approach_info":"geo_location"::TEXT != 'CRITERIA_UNUSED'
  AND f."audience_selection_approach_info":"contextual_signals"::TEXT != 'CRITERIA_UNUSED'
  AND f."audience_selection_approach_info":"customer_lists"::TEXT != 'CRITERIA_UNUSED'
  AND f."audience_selection_approach_info":"topics_of_interest"::TEXT != 'CRITERIA_UNUSED'
ORDER BY f."region_entry":"times_shown_upper_bound"::INTEGER DESC
LIMIT 1;
```
</details>

```sql
WITH 
-- Get sorafenib drug ID
sorafenib_drug AS (
    SELECT DISTINCT drugID
    FROM `isb-cgc-bq.targetome_versioned.drug_synonyms_v1`
    WHERE LOWER(synonym) LIKE '%sorafenib%'
),

-- Get sorafenib targets with filtered assay conditions
sorafenib_targets AS (
    SELECT DISTINCT i.targetID, i.target_uniprotID
    FROM `isb-cgc-bq.targetome_versioned.interactions_v1` i
    INNER JOIN sorafenib_drug sd ON i.drugID = sd.drugID
    INNER JOIN `isb-cgc-bq.targetome_versioned.experiments_v1` e ON i.expID = e.expID
    WHERE i.targetSpecies = 'Homo sapiens'
      AND i.target_uniprotID IS NOT NULL
      AND e.exp_assayValueMedian IS NOT NULL
      AND e.exp_assayValueMedian <= 100
      AND (e.exp_assayValueLow IS NULL OR e.exp_assayValueLow <= 100)
      AND (e.exp_assayValueHigh IS NULL OR e.exp_assayValueHigh <= 100)
),

-- Get all lowest-level Homo sapiens pathways  
lowest_human_pathways AS (
    SELECT stable_id, name
    FROM `isb-cgc-bq.reactome_versioned.pathway_v77`
    WHERE lowest_level = TRUE
      AND species = 'Homo sapiens'
),

-- Get TAS evidence physical entities in these pathways
pathway_tas_entities AS (
    SELECT DISTINCT pp.pathway_stable_id, pe.uniprot_id
    FROM `isb-cgc-bq.reactome_versioned.pe_to_pathway_v77` pp
    INNER JOIN lowest_human_pathways lhp ON pp.pathway_stable_id = lhp.stable_id
    INNER JOIN `isb-cgc-bq.reactome_versioned.physical_entity_v77` pe 
        ON pp.pe_stable_id = pe.stable_id
    WHERE pp.evidence_code = 'TAS'
      AND pe.uniprot_id IS NOT NULL
),

-- Count total sorafenib targets
target_counts AS (
    SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT target_uniprotID) AS total_targets
    FROM sorafenib_targets
),

-- For each pathway, calculate contingency table
pathway_contingency AS (
    SELECT 
        lhp.stable_id AS pathway_id,
        lhp.name,
        -- a: targets in pathway
        COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN st.target_uniprotID = pte.uniprot_id 
             THEN st.target_uniprotID END) AS targets_in_pathway,
        -- b: targets not in pathway (total targets - targets in pathway)
        (SELECT total_targets FROM target_counts) - 
        COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN st.target_uniprotID = pte.uniprot_id 
             THEN st.target_uniprotID END) AS targets_out_pathway,
        -- c: non-targets in pathway (total TAS entities in pathway - targets in pathway)
        COUNT(DISTINCT pte.uniprot_id) - 
        COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN st.target_uniprotID = pte.uniprot_id 
             THEN st.target_uniprotID END) AS non_targets_in_pathway,
        -- d: non-targets not in pathway (total human TAS entities - total TAS entities in pathway)
        (SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT uniprot_id) FROM pathway_tas_entities) - 
        COUNT(DISTINCT pte.uniprot_id) AS non_targets_out_pathway
    FROM lowest_human_pathways lhp
    LEFT JOIN pathway_tas_entities pte ON lhp.stable_id = pte.pathway_stable_id
    LEFT JOIN sorafenib_targets st ON pte.uniprot_id = st.target_uniprotID
    GROUP BY lhp.stable_id, lhp.name
),

-- Calculate chi-squared statistic for each pathway
pathway_chisq AS (
    SELECT 
        name,
        targets_in_pathway,
        targets_out_pathway,
        non_targets_in_pathway,
        non_targets_out_pathway,
        ROUND(
            CASE 
                WHEN (targets_in_pathway + targets_out_pathway) > 0 
                 AND (non_targets_in_pathway + non_targets_out_pathway) > 0
                 AND (targets_in_pathway + non_targets_in_pathway) > 0
                 AND (targets_out_pathway + non_targets_out_pathway) > 0
                THEN 
                    (targets_in_pathway * non_targets_out_pathway - targets_out_pathway * non_targets_in_pathway) *
                    (targets_in_pathway * non_targets_out_pathway - targets_out_pathway * non_targets_in_pathway) /
                    ((targets_in_pathway + targets_out_pathway) * 
                     (non_targets_in_pathway + non_targets_out_pathway) *
                     (targets_in_pathway + non_targets_in_pathway) *
                     (targets_out_pathway + non_targets_out_pathway))
                ELSE 0
            END, 4
        ) AS chi_squared
    FROM pathway_contingency
)

-- Top 3 pathways by chi-squared
SELECT 
    name AS pathway_name,
    targets_in_pathway,
    targets_out_pathway,
    non_targets_in_pathway,
    non_targets_out_pathway,
    chi_squared
FROM pathway_chisq
ORDER BY chi_squared DESC
LIMIT 3;
```

```sql
WITH
-- 1. Distinct human targets of sorafenib satisfying assay conditions
sorafenib_targets AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT i.target_uniprotID AS uniprot
  FROM `isb-cgc-bq.targetome_versioned.interactions_v1` i
  JOIN `isb-cgc-bq.targetome_versioned.experiments_v1` e
    ON i.expID = e.expID
  WHERE LOWER(i.drugName) = 'sorafenib'
    AND i.targetSpecies = 'Homo sapiens'
    AND e.exp_assayValueMedian <= 100
    AND (e.exp_assayValueLow   <= 100 OR e.exp_assayValueLow   IS NULL)
    AND (e.exp_assayValueHigh  <= 100 OR e.exp_assayValueHigh  IS NULL)
),

-- 2. All human UniProt IDs that appear in any human Reactome pathway
human_pe_universe AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT pe.uniprot_id AS uniprot
  FROM `isb-cgc-bq.reactome_versioned.physical_entity_v77` pe
  JOIN `isb-cgc-bq.reactome_versioned.pe_to_pathway_v77` pep
    ON pe.stable_id = pep.pe_stable_id
  JOIN `isb-cgc-bq.reactome_versioned.pathway_v77` pw
    ON pep.pathway_stable_id = pw.stable_id
  WHERE pw.species = 'Homo sapiens'
    AND pe.uniprot_id IS NOT NULL
),

-- 3. For each lowest‑level human pathway with TAS evidence, list its member UniProt IDs
pathway_pe_uniprot AS (
  SELECT pw.stable_id   AS pathway_id,
         pw.name        AS pathway_name,
         pe.uniprot_id  AS uniprot
  FROM `isb-cgc-bq.reactome_versioned.pathway_v77` pw
  JOIN `isb-cgc-bq.reactome_versioned.pe_to_pathway_v77` pep
    ON pw.stable_id = pep.pathway_stable_id
  JOIN `isb-cgc-bq.reactome_versioned.physical_entity_v77` pe
    ON pep.pe_stable_id = pe.stable_id
  WHERE pw.lowest_level = TRUE
    AND pw.species      = 'Homo sapiens'
    AND pep.evidence_code = 'TAS'
    AND pe.uniprot_id IS NOT NULL
),

-- 4. Per pathway counts: total members and sorafenib target members
pathway_stats AS (
  SELECT p.pathway_id,
         p.pathway_name,
         COUNT(DISTINCT p.uniprot)                                  AS total_in_pathway,
         COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN s.uniprot IS NOT NULL
                              THEN p.uniprot END)                  AS targets_in_pathway
  FROM pathway_pe_uniprot p
  LEFT JOIN sorafenib_targets s
    ON p.uniprot = s.uniprot
  GROUP BY p.pathway_id, p.pathway_name
),

-- 5. Global counts needed for chi‑squared calculation
overall_counts AS (
  SELECT
    (SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT uniprot) FROM sorafenib_targets) AS total_targets,
    (SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT uniprot) FROM human_pe_universe) AS total_universe
)

-- 6. Compute chi‑squared for each pathway, keep top 3, and output the requested counts
SELECT
  ps.pathway_name,
  ps.targets_in_pathway   AS targets_within_pathway,
  oc.total_targets - ps.targets_in_pathway   AS targets_outside_pathway,
  ps.total_in_pathway - ps.targets_in_pathway   AS nontargets_within_pathway,
  oc.total_universe - ps.total_in_pathway - (oc.total_targets - ps.targets_in_pathway) AS nontargets_outside_pathway
  -- Chi‑squared value is included for transparency (not explicitly requested)
  -- , ROUND(
  --   ( (ps.targets_in_pathway * 
  --        (oc.total_universe - ps.total_in_pathway - (oc.total_targets - ps.targets_in_pathway))
  --      - (oc.total_targets - ps.targets_in_pathway) * (ps.total_in_pathway - ps.targets_in_pathway)
  --     )^2 * oc.total_universe
  --   ) / NULLIF(
  --     ( (ps.targets_in_pathway + (oc.total_targets - ps.targets_in_pathway)) *
  --       (ps.total_in_pathway + (oc.total_universe - ps.total_in_pathway)) *
  --       (ps.targets_in_pathway + (ps.total_in_pathway - ps.targets_in_pathway)) *
  --       ((oc.total_targets - ps.targets_in_pathway) + 
  --        (oc.total_universe - ps.total_in_pathway - (oc.total_targets - ps.targets_in_pathway)))
  --     ), 0
  --   ), 4
  -- ) AS chi_squared
FROM pathway_stats ps
CROSS JOIN overall_counts oc
ORDER BY
  -- Order by chi‑squared descending (computed inline with the same formula)
  ( (ps.targets_in_pathway * 
        (oc.total_universe - ps.total_in_pathway - (oc.total_targets - ps.targets_in_pathway))
      - (oc.total_targets - ps.targets_in_pathway) * (ps.total_in_pathway - ps.targets_in_pathway)
    )^2 * oc.total_universe
  ) / NULLIF(
    ( (ps.targets_in_pathway + (oc.total_targets - ps.targets_in_pathway)) *
      (ps.total_in_pathway + (oc.total_universe - ps.total_in_pathway)) *
      (ps.targets_in_pathway + (ps.total_in_pathway - ps.targets_in_pathway)) *
      ((oc.total_targets - ps.targets_in_pathway) + 
       (oc.total_universe - ps.total_in_pathway - (oc.total_targets - ps.targets_in_pathway)))
    ), 0
  ) DESC
LIMIT 3;
```

<summary><b>View Baseline SQL (❌)</b></summary>

```sql
-- This query finds the top 10 countries by the latest available long-term external debt,
-- excluding entries without a specified region (i.e., region is NULL or 'None').
-- Uses the standard World Bank indicator code 'DT.DOD.DLXF.CD' for long-term external debt stocks.

WITH latest_debt AS (
  -- For each country, get the most recent year's value for long-term external debt
  SELECT
    country_code,
    value,
    year
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.world_bank_intl_debt.international_debt`
  WHERE indicator_code = 'DT.DOD.DLXF.CD'
    AND value IS NOT NULL         -- exclude missing or NaN values
  QUALIFY ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY country_code ORDER BY year DESC) = 1
)

SELECT
  cs.short_name AS country,
  ld.value AS total_long_term_external_debt
FROM latest_debt ld
JOIN `bigquery-public-data.world_bank_intl_debt.country_summary` cs
  ON ld.country_code = cs.country_code
WHERE
  cs.region IS NOT NULL
  AND cs.region != 'None'          -- exclude aggregates and regions without a defined region
ORDER BY ld.value DESC
LIMIT 10;
```
</details>

<details>
<summary><b>View SlayQL SQL (❌)</b></summary>

```sql
-- Step 1: Identify the indicator for long-term external debt.
-- We use indicator_code 'DT.DOD.DLXF.CD' (External debt stocks, long-term, current US$).
-- Step 2: Join the debt data with the country_summary table to obtain region information.
-- Step 3: Exclude rows where region is 'None' (i.e., regional aggregates).
-- Step 4: Aggregate by country, summing the debt values over all available years.
-- Step 5: Order by total debt descending and return the top 10 countries.

WITH filtered_debt AS (
  SELECT 
    d.country_code,
    d.country_name,
    d.value
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.world_bank_intl_debt.international_debt` d
  INNER JOIN `bigquery-public-data.world_bank_intl_debt.country_summary` c
    ON d.country_code = c.country_code
  WHERE d.indicator_code = 'DT.DOD.DLXF.CD'
    -- Filter out rows with missing or non-country regions
    AND c.region IS NOT NULL
    AND c.region != 'None'
    -- Exclude null/NaN debt values
    AND d.value IS NOT NULL
    AND NOT IS_NAN(d.value)
)
SELECT 
  country_name,
  ROUND(SUM(value), 4) AS total_long_term_external_debt
FROM filtered_debt
GROUP BY country_name, country_code
ORDER BY total_long_term_external_debt DESC
LIMIT 10;
```
</details>

### 106. bq229 (DB: `open_images`)
**Question**: Using the bigquery-public-data.open_images dataset, can you provide a count of how many distinct image URLs are categorized as 'cat' (where the image has label '/m/01yrx' with confidence=1) and how many distinct image URLs are categorized as 'other' (meaning they have no cat label '/m/01yrx' at all)?

**Status**: Baseline ❌ | SlayQL ❌

#### 📊 Execution Results Comparison

<details open>
<summary><b>Gold Standard Result (Expected)</b></summary>

| category   |   url_count |
|:-----------|------------:|
| cat        |       40231 |
| other      |     9122224 |

**OR**

|   cat_count |   other_count |
|------------:|--------------:|
|       40231 |   9.12222e+06 |

</details>

<details open>
<summary><b>SlayQL Execution Result (❌)</b></summary>

N/A

</details>

<details open>
<summary><b>Baseline Execution Result (❌)</b></summary>

|   cat_image_url_count |   other_image_url_count |
|----------------------:|------------------------:|
|                 40231 |             9.13804e+06 |

</details>

#### 📜 Generated SQL Queries

<details>
<summary><b>View Baseline SQL (❌)</b></summary>

```sql
-- Step 1: Identify all image_ids that have the cat label '/m/01yrx' with confidence=1
WITH cat_images AS (
    SELECT DISTINCT image_id
    FROM `bigquery-public-data.open_images.labels`
    WHERE label_name = '/m/01yrx'
      AND confidence = 1
),

-- Step 2: Count distinct image URLs for cat and non-cat images
cat_count AS (
    SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT img.original_url) AS cat_url_count
    FROM `bigquery-public-data.open_images.images` img
    INNER JOIN cat_images ci ON img.image_id = ci.image_id
),

other_count AS (
    SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT img.original_url) AS other_url_count
    FROM `bigquery-public-data.open_images.images` img
    WHERE img.image_id NOT IN (SELECT image_id FROM cat_images)
)

-- Step 3: Return both counts in a single row
SELECT 
    cat_url_count AS cat_image_url_count,
    other_url_count AS other_image_url_count
FROM cat_count, other_count;
```
</details>

<details>
<summary><b>View SlayQL SQL (❌)</b></summary>

```sql
-- Final complete SQL query
WITH 
-- Get all image URLs that are labeled as 'cat' with exactly confidence=1
cat_images AS (
    SELECT DISTINCT i.image_url
    FROM `bigquery-public-data.open_images.images` i
    INNER JOIN `bigquery-public-data.open_images.train_annotations` a 
        ON i.image_id = a.image_id
    WHERE a.label_id = '/m/01yrx' 
      AND a.confidence = 1
),

-- Get all image URLs that have ANY cat label (at any confidence level)
-- This is needed to determine 'other' images that have no cat label at all
cat_any_images AS (
    SELECT DISTINCT i.image_url
    FROM `bigquery-public-data.open_images.images` i
    INNER JOIN `bigquery-public-data.open_images.train_annotations` a 
        ON i.image_id = a.image_id
    WHERE a.label_id = '/m/01yrx'
),

-- Get all distinct image URLs from the entire dataset
all_images AS (
    SELECT DISTINCT image_url
    FROM `bigquery-public-data.open_images.images`
)

-- Final selection: Count cat images and other images separately
SELECT 
    'cat' AS category,
    COUNT(DISTINCT image_url) AS image_count
FROM cat_images
UNION ALL
SELECT 
    'other' AS category,
    COUNT(DISTINCT image_url) AS image_count
FROM (
    SELECT image_url 
    FROM all_images
    EXCEPT DISTINCT
    SELECT image_url 
    FROM cat_any_images
)
```
</details>
