#### 📜 Generated SQL Queries

<details>
<summary><b>View Baseline SQL (❌)</b></summary>

```sql
-- Step 1: Find the forum ID for "General"
WITH general_forum AS (
    SELECT "Id"
    FROM META_KAGGLE.META_KAGGLE.FORUMS
    WHERE LOWER("Title") = 'general'
),

-- Step 2: Find all sub-forums under General (forums whose ParentForumId = General's Id)
sub_forums AS (
    SELECT f."Id" AS "sub_forum_id",
           f."Title" AS "sub_forum_title"
    FROM META_KAGGLE.META_KAGGLE.FORUMS f
    JOIN general_forum g ON f."ParentForumId" = g."Id"
),

-- Step 3: Get the earliest five topics in those sub-forums
topics AS (
    SELECT t."Id" AS "topic_id",
           t."CreationDate",
           t."Title" AS "topic_title",
           t."ForumId",
           t."TotalViews"
    FROM META_KAGGLE.META_KAGGLE.FORUMTOPICS t
    JOIN sub_forums s ON t."ForumId" = s."sub_forum_id"
    ORDER BY t."CreationDate" ASC
    LIMIT 5
),

-- Step 4: Compute per-topic message counts and distinct users
message_stats AS (
    SELECT m."ForumTopicId",
           COUNT(*) AS "reply_count",
           COUNT(DISTINCT m."PostUserId") AS "distinct_user_replies_count"
    FROM META_KAGGLE.META_KAGGLE.FORUMMESSAGES m
    JOIN topics t ON m."ForumTopicId" = t."topic_id"
    GROUP BY m."ForumTopicId"
),

-- Step 5: Compute total upvotes per topic (each vote is an upvote)
vote_stats AS (
    SELECT m."ForumTopicId",
           COUNT(v."Id") AS "total_upvotes"
    FROM META_KAGGLE.META_KAGGLE.FORUMMESSAGES m
    JOIN META_KAGGLE.META_KAGGLE.FORUMMESSAGEVOTES v
         ON m."Id" = v."ForumMessageId"
    JOIN topics t ON m."ForumTopicId" = t."topic_id"
    GROUP BY m."ForumTopicId"
)

-- Step 6: Final selection with coalesce for missing values
SELECT
    t."CreationDate",
    t."topic_title" AS "Title",
    s."sub_forum_title" AS "Parent Forum Title",
    COALESCE(ms."reply_count", 0) AS "Reply count",
    COALESCE(ms."distinct_user_replies_count", 0) AS "Distinct user replies count",
    COALESCE(vs."total_upvotes", 0) AS "Total upvotes",
    COALESCE(t."TotalViews", 0) AS "Total views"
FROM topics t
LEFT JOIN sub_forums s ON t."ForumId" = s."sub_forum_id"
LEFT JOIN message_stats ms ON t."topic_id" = ms."ForumTopicId"
LEFT JOIN vote_stats vs ON t."topic_id" = vs."ForumTopicId"
ORDER BY t."CreationDate" ASC;
```
</details>

<details>
<summary><b>View SlayQL SQL (❌)</b></summary>

```sql
-- Step 1: Identify the parent forum "General" and get its id
WITH "general_forum" AS (
    SELECT "id"
    FROM "META_KAGGLE"."META_KAGGLE"."FORUMS"
    WHERE LOWER("Title") LIKE '%general%'
),

-- Step 2: Get all sub-forums (children) of the General forum
"sub_forums" AS (
    SELECT "id" AS "forum_id"
    FROM "META_KAGGLE"."META_KAGGLE"."FORUMS"
    WHERE "ParentForumId" IN (SELECT "id" FROM "general_forum")
),

-- Step 3: Get the earliest 5 topics from any sub-forum under General
"earliest_topics" AS (
    SELECT 
        t."id" AS "topic_id",
        t."CreationDate",
        t."Title",
        f."Title" AS "parent_forum_title",
        t."ForumId",
        t."ViewCount"
    FROM "META_KAGGLE"."META_KAGGLE"."FORUMTOPICS" t
    INNER JOIN "META_KAGGLE"."META_KAGGLE"."FORUMS" f
        ON t."ForumId" = f."id"
    WHERE f."id" IN (SELECT "forum_id" FROM "sub_forums")
    ORDER BY t."CreationDate" ASC
    LIMIT 5
),

-- Step 4: Aggregate reply and user metrics per topic
"topic_metrics" AS (
    SELECT 
        et."topic_id",
        et."CreationDate",
        et."Title",
        et."parent_forum_title",
        COALESCE(COUNT(m."id"), 0) AS "reply_count",
        COALESCE(COUNT(DISTINCT m."UserId"), 0) AS "distinct_user_replies_count",
        COALESCE(COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN m."VoteType" = 'Upvote' THEN m."id" END), 0) AS "total_upvotes",
        -- Note: ViewCount is already in the topic table
        COALESCE(et."ViewCount", 0) AS "total_views"
    FROM "earliest_topics" et
    LEFT JOIN "META_KAGGLE"."META_KAGGLE"."FORUMMESSAGES" m
        ON et."topic_id" = m."TopicId"
    GROUP BY 
        et."topic_id",
        et."CreationDate",
        et."Title",
        et."parent_forum_title",
        et."ViewCount"
)

-- Step 5: Final output with required fields
SELECT 
    "CreationDate",
    "Title",
    "parent_forum_title",
    "reply_count",
    "distinct_user_replies_count",
    "total_upvotes",
    "total_views"
FROM "topic_metrics"
ORDER BY "CreationDate" ASC;
```
</details>

### 108. sf_bq372 (DB: `WIDE_WORLD_IMPORTERS`)
**Question**: Among all orders that do not appear in the invoice table, for each customer category calculate the maximum lost order value, then determine which customer category’s maximum lost order value is closest to the overall average of these maximum lost order values across all categories?

**Status**: Baseline ❌ | SlayQL ❌

#### 📊 Execution Results Comparison

<details open>
<summary><b>Gold Standard Result (Expected)</b></summary>

| CustomerCategoryName   |   MaxLostOrderValue |   AvgMaxLostOrderValue |   DifferenceFromAverage |
|:-----------------------|--------------------:|-----------------------:|------------------------:|
| Gift Store             |                5040 |                 4995.2 |                    44.8 |

**OR**

|   CustomerCategoryID | CustomerCategoryName   |   MAX_LOST_ORDER_VALUE |   AVG_OF_MAXES |   DIFF_FROM_AVG |
|---------------------:|:-----------------------|-----------------------:|---------------:|----------------:|
|                    6 | Gift Store             |                   5796 |        5744.48 |           51.52 |

**OR**

|   CustomerCategoryID | CustomerCategoryName   |   max_lost_order_value |   distance_to_avg |
|---------------------:|:-----------------------|-----------------------:|------------------:|
|                    6 | Gift Store             |                   5796 |             51.52 |

</details>

<details open>
<summary><b>SlayQL Execution Result (❌)</b></summary>

N/A

</details>

<details open>
<summary><b>Baseline Execution Result (❌)</b></summary>

| CustomerCategoryName   |
|:-----------------------|
| Gift Store             |

</details>

#### 📜 Generated SQL Queries

<details>
<summary><b>View Baseline SQL (❌)</b></summary>

```sql
WITH 
-- Step 1: Find orders not in invoices and calculate their total value
"non_invoiced_orders" AS (
    SELECT 
        so."OrderID",
        so."CustomerID",
        SUM(sol."Quantity" * sol."UnitPrice") AS "order_value"
    FROM "WIDE_WORLD_IMPORTERS"."WIDE_WORLD_IMPORTERS"."SALES_ORDERS" so
    INNER JOIN "WIDE_WORLD_IMPORTERS"."WIDE_WORLD_IMPORTERS"."SALES_ORDERLINES" sol 
        ON so."OrderID" = sol."OrderID"
    WHERE NOT EXISTS (
        SELECT 1 
        FROM "WIDE_WORLD_IMPORTERS"."WIDE_WORLD_IMPORTERS"."SALES_INVOICES" si
        WHERE si."OrderID" = so."OrderID"
    )
    GROUP BY so."OrderID", so."CustomerID"
),

-- Step 2: Get max lost order value per customer category
"max_per_category" AS (
    SELECT 
        cc."CustomerCategoryID",
        cc."CustomerCategoryName",
        MAX(nio."order_value") AS "max_lost_value"
    FROM "non_invoiced_orders" nio
    INNER JOIN "WIDE_WORLD_IMPORTERS"."WIDE_WORLD_IMPORTERS"."SALES_CUSTOMERS" c 
        ON nio."CustomerID" = c."CustomerID"
    INNER JOIN "WIDE_WORLD_IMPORTERS"."WIDE_WORLD_IMPORTERS"."SALES_CUSTOMERCATEGORIES" cc 
        ON c."CustomerCategoryID" = cc."CustomerCategoryID"
    GROUP BY cc."CustomerCategoryID", cc."CustomerCategoryName"
),

-- Step 3: Calculate overall average of max lost values
"overall_avg" AS (
    SELECT AVG("max_lost_value") AS "avg_max_lost_value"
    FROM "max_per_category"
)

-- Step 4: Find which category's max is closest to the average
SELECT 
    mpc."CustomerCategoryName" AS "CustomerCategoryName"
FROM "max_per_category" mpc
CROSS JOIN "overall_avg" oa
ORDER BY ABS(mpc."max_lost_value" - oa."avg_max_lost_value")
LIMIT 1;
```

<details>
<summary><b>View SlayQL SQL (❌)</b></summary>

```sql
WITH
-- Step 1: Identify orders that do NOT appear in the invoice table
lost_orders AS (
    SELECT
        so."OrderID",
        so."CustomerID"
    FROM "WIDE_WORLD_IMPORTERS"."WIDE_WORLD_IMPORTERS"."SALES_ORDERS" so
    LEFT JOIN "WIDE_WORLD_IMPORTERS"."WIDE_WORLD_IMPORTERS"."SALES_INVOICES" si
        ON so."OrderID" = si."OrderID"
    WHERE si."InvoiceID" IS NULL
),

-- Step 2: Calculate the total value (Quantity * UnitPrice) for each lost order
order_values AS (
    SELECT
        lo."OrderID",
        SUM(sol."Quantity" * sol."UnitPrice") AS lost_order_value
    FROM lost_orders lo
    INNER JOIN "WIDE_WORLD_IMPORTERS"."WIDE_WORLD_IMPORTERS"."SALES_ORDERLINES" sol
        ON lo."OrderID" = sol."OrderID"
    GROUP BY lo."OrderID"
),

-- Step 3: For each customer category, calculate the maximum lost order value
category_max_values AS (
    SELECT
        cc."CustomerCategoryName",
        MAX(ov.lost_order_value) AS max_lost_value
    FROM order_values ov
    INNER JOIN lost_orders lo
        ON ov."OrderID" = lo."OrderID"
    INNER JOIN "WIDE_WORLD_IMPORTERS"."WIDE_WORLD_IMPORTERS"."SALES_CUSTOMERS" c
        ON lo."CustomerID" = c."CustomerID"
    INNER JOIN "WIDE_WORLD_IMPORTERS"."WIDE_WORLD_IMPORTERS"."SALES_CUSTOMERCATEGORIES" cc
        ON c."CustomerCategoryID" = cc."CustomerCategoryID"
    GROUP BY cc."CustomerCategoryName"
),

-- Step 4: Compute the overall average of these per-category maximum values
overall_avg AS (
    SELECT AVG(max_lost_value) AS avg_max_lost_value
    FROM category_max_values
)

-- Step 5: Determine which customer category's max value is closest to the overall average
SELECT
    cm."CustomerCategoryName" AS customer_category
FROM category_max_values cm
CROSS JOIN overall_avg oa
ORDER BY ROUND(ABS(cm.max_lost_value - oa.avg_max_lost_value), 4)
LIMIT 1;
```

### 109. bq393 (DB: `hacker_news`)
**Question**: I want to identify users who had activity followed by inactivity. Specifically, find the user ID and their corresponding month number (counting from their first activity month) for the user with the highest month number who became inactive (no activity recorded) after their last recorded activity month. For this analysis, only consider data up until September 10, 2024, and ensure the month number represents the count of months since the user's first activity. The user should have at least one month where they were expected to be active (within their activity span) but actually had no records.

**Status**: Baseline ❌ | SlayQL ❌

#### 📊 Execution Results Comparison

#### 📜 Generated SQL Queries

<summary><b>View Baseline SQL (❌)</b></summary>

```sql
WITH 
-- Get distinct year-month combinations for each user's activity
user_activity_months AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT
    by AS user_id,
    EXTRACT(YEAR FROM timestamp) AS activity_year,
    EXTRACT(MONTH FROM timestamp) AS activity_month,
    -- Create a date representation for ordering
    DATE_TRUNC(DATE(timestamp), MONTH) AS activity_month_date
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.hacker_news.full`
  WHERE 
    by IS NOT NULL
    AND by != 'None'
    AND (deleted IS NULL OR deleted = FALSE)
    AND (dead IS NULL OR dead = FALSE)
    AND timestamp <= '2024-09-10 23:59:59+00:00'
),

-- Get each user's first and last activity month
user_activity_range AS (
  SELECT
    user_id,
    MIN(activity_month_date) AS first_activity_month,
    MAX(activity_month_date) AS last_activity_month,
    -- Calculate total months span
    DATE_DIFF(MAX(activity_month_date), MIN(activity_month_date), MONTH) AS total_months_span
  FROM user_activity_months
  GROUP BY user_id
  HAVING first_activity_month < last_activity_month  -- User must have at least 2 months of activity
),

-- Generate all expected months for each user
-- Using a numbers table approach for month generation
all_users_expected_months AS (
  SELECT
    r.user_id,
    r.first_activity_month,
    r.last_activity_month,
    -- Generate month number (1-based from first activity)
    offset + 1 AS month_number,
    DATE_ADD(r.first_activity_month, INTERVAL offset MONTH) AS expected_month
  FROM user_activity_range r
  CROSS JOIN UNNEST(GENERATE_ARRAY(0, r.total_months_span)) AS offset
),

-- Find months where user had no activity
inactive_months AS (
  SELECT
    e.user_id,
    e.month_number,
    e.expected_month
  FROM all_users_expected_months e
  LEFT JOIN user_activity_months a
    ON e.user_id = a.user_id
    AND e.expected_month = a.activity_month_date
  WHERE a.user_id IS NULL  -- No activity in this month
)

-- Get the user with the highest month number who had inactivity
SELECT
  user_id,
  MAX(month_number) AS highest_inactive_month_number
FROM inactive_months
GROUP BY user_id
ORDER BY highest_inactive_month_number DESC
LIMIT 1;
```

<details>
<summary><b>View SlayQL SQL (❌)</b></summary>

```sql
WITH 
-- Step 1: Get distinct user activity months up to Sep 10, 2024
user_activity_months AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT
    `by` AS user_id,
    DATE_TRUNC(DATE(timestamp), MONTH) AS activity_month
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.hacker_news.full`
  WHERE `by` IS NOT NULL 
    AND LOWER(TRIM(`by`)) != 'none'
    AND `by` != ''
    AND timestamp <= TIMESTAMP('2024-09-10')
),

-- Step 2: Compute first, last, count of active months, and span months for each user
user_first_last AS (
  SELECT
    user_id,
    MIN(activity_month) AS first_month,
    MAX(activity_month) AS last_month,
    COUNT(DISTINCT activity_month) AS num_active_months,
    1 + DATE_DIFF(MAX(activity_month), MIN(activity_month), MONTH) AS span_months
  FROM user_activity_months
  GROUP BY user_id
),

-- Step 3: Users who became inactive after last activity
-- Exclude users whose last activity is in Sep 2024 (cutoff month, can't verify inactivity)
users_inactive_after AS (
  SELECT
    ufl.user_id,
    ufl.first_month,
    ufl.last_month,
    ufl.num_active_months,
    ufl.span_months
  FROM user_first_last ufl
  WHERE ufl.last_month < DATE_TRUNC(DATE('2024-09-10'), MONTH)
    AND NOT EXISTS (
      SELECT 1
      FROM user_activity_months uam
      WHERE uam.user_id = ufl.user_id
        AND uam.activity_month > ufl.last_month
    )
),

-- Step 4: Users with at least one gap within their activity span
users_with_gaps AS (
  SELECT
    uia.user_id,
    uia.first_month,
    uia.last_month
  FROM users_inactive_after uia
  WHERE uia.num_active_months < uia.span_months
),

-- Step 5: Compute month number (counting from first activity month = 1)
users_final AS (
  SELECT
    uwg.user_id,
    DATE_DIFF(uwg.last_month, uwg.first_month, MONTH) + 1 AS month_number
  FROM users_with_gaps uwg
)

-- Step 6: Get the user with the highest month number
SELECT
  user_id,
  month_number
FROM users_final
ORDER BY month_number DESC
LIMIT 1;
```
</details>

#### 📜 Generated SQL Queries

<details>
<summary><b>View Baseline SQL (❌)</b></summary>

```sql
-- Compute median revenue and median functional expenses per year (2012-2017)
-- using APPROX_QUANTILES for efficiency, then compute the absolute difference
-- and select the three years with the smallest difference.

WITH all_years AS (
  -- Union all main 990 tables for 2012-2017, standardizing tax_pd as string
  SELECT 
    CAST(tax_pd AS STRING) AS tax_pd_str,
    totrevenue,
    totfuncexpns
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.irs_990.irs_990_2012`
  UNION ALL
  SELECT 
    CAST(tax_pd AS STRING),
    totrevenue,
    totfuncexpns
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.irs_990.irs_990_2013`
  UNION ALL
  SELECT 
    CAST(tax_pd AS STRING),
    totrevenue,
    totfuncexpns
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.irs_990.irs_990_2014`
  UNION ALL
  SELECT 
    CAST(tax_pd AS STRING),
    totrevenue,
    totfuncexpns
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.irs_990.irs_990_2015`
  UNION ALL
  SELECT 
    CAST(tax_pd AS STRING),
    totrevenue,
    totfuncexpns
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.irs_990.irs_990_2016`
  UNION ALL
  SELECT 
    CAST(tax_pd AS STRING),
    totrevenue,
    totfuncexpns
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.irs_990.irs_990_2017`
),
with_year AS (
  -- Extract the calendar year from tax_period (first 4 characters)
  -- and keep only non‑null financial values
  SELECT 
    SAFE_CAST(SUBSTR(tax_pd_str, 1, 4) AS INT64) AS year,
    totrevenue,
    totfuncexpns
  FROM all_years
  WHERE SAFE_CAST(SUBSTR(tax_pd_str, 1, 4) AS INT64) BETWEEN 2012 AND 2017
    AND totrevenue IS NOT NULL
    AND totfuncexpns IS NOT NULL
),
medians AS (
  -- Compute median revenue and median expenses per year
  SELECT 
    year,
    APPROX_QUANTILES(totrevenue, 100)[OFFSET(50)] AS median_revenue,
    APPROX_QUANTILES(totfuncexpns, 100)[OFFSET(50)] AS median_func_expenses
  FROM with_year
  GROUP BY year
)
-- Output the three years with the smallest absolute difference
SELECT 
  year,
  ABS(median_revenue - median_func_expenses) AS diff
FROM medians
ORDER BY diff ASC
LIMIT 3
```
</details>

<details>
<summary><b>View SlayQL SQL (❌)</b></summary>

```sql
WITH yearly_data AS (
  SELECT
    CAST(_TABLE_SUFFIX AS INT64) AS year,
    totrevenue,
    totfuncexpns
  FROM `bigquery-public-data.irs_990.irs_990_*`
  WHERE REGEXP_CONTAINS(_TABLE_SUFFIX, r'^\d{4}$')
    AND _TABLE_SUFFIX BETWEEN '2012' AND '2017'
    AND totrevenue IS NOT NULL
    AND totfuncexpns IS NOT NULL
),
medians AS (
  SELECT
    year,
    PERCENTILE_CONT(totrevenue, 0.5) OVER(PARTITION BY year) AS median_revenue,
    PERCENTILE_CONT(totfuncexpns, 0.5) OVER(PARTITION BY year) AS median_func_expenses
  FROM yearly_data
)
SELECT DISTINCT
  year,
  ABS(median_revenue - median_func_expenses) AS abs_diff
FROM medians
ORDER BY abs_diff
LIMIT 3;
```
</details>

#### 📜 Generated SQL Queries

<details>
<summary><b>View Baseline SQL (❌)</b></summary>

```sql
WITH
    -- Step 1: Identify race codes that describe 'black' (case-insensitive)
    black_race_codes AS (
        SELECT "Code"
        FROM "DEATH"."DEATH"."RACE"
        WHERE LOWER("Description") LIKE '%black%'
    ),

    -- Step 2: Identify ICD-10 codes whose description contains 'vehicle'
    vehicle_icd_codes AS (
        SELECT "Code"
        FROM "DEATH"."DEATH"."ICD10CODE"
        WHERE LOWER("Description") LIKE '%vehicle%'
    ),

    -- Step 3: Identify ICD-10 codes whose description contains 'firearm'
    firearm_icd_codes AS (
        SELECT "Code"
        FROM "DEATH"."DEATH"."ICD10CODE"
        WHERE LOWER("Description") LIKE '%firearm%'
    ),

    -- Step 4: Find all death records associated with at least one vehicle ICD code
    vehicle_death_records AS (
        SELECT DISTINCT "DeathRecordId"
        FROM "DEATH"."DEATH"."ENTITYAXISCONDITIONS"
        WHERE "Icd10Code" IN (SELECT "Code" FROM vehicle_icd_codes)
    ),

    -- Step 5: Find all death records associated with at least one firearm ICD code
    firearm_death_records AS (
        SELECT DISTINCT "DeathRecordId"
        FROM "DEATH"."DEATH"."ENTITYAXISCONDITIONS"
        WHERE "Icd10Code" IN (SELECT "Code" FROM firearm_icd_codes)
    ),

    -- Step 6: Combine both causes into a single list with a cause label
    all_death_ids AS (
        SELECT "DeathRecordId", 'Vehicle' AS "cause"
        FROM vehicle_death_records
        UNION ALL
        SELECT "DeathRecordId", 'Firearm' AS "cause"
        FROM firearm_death_records
    ),

    -- Step 7: Attach age and race information, restrict to ages 12-18 (in years)
    deaths_with_cause AS (
        SELECT
            d."Id",
            d."Age",
            d."Race",
            a."cause"
        FROM "DEATH"."DEATH"."DEATHRECORDS" d
        INNER JOIN all_death_ids a ON d."Id" = a."DeathRecordId"
        WHERE d."AgeType" = 1           -- Age is in years
          AND d."Age" BETWEEN 12 AND 18
    ),

    -- Step 8: Generate all ages 12 through 18 inclusive
    age_series AS (
        SELECT 12 AS "age"
        UNION ALL SELECT 13
        UNION ALL SELECT 14
        UNION ALL SELECT 15
        UNION ALL SELECT 16
        UNION ALL SELECT 17
        UNION ALL SELECT 18
    ),

    -- Step 9: Create all combinations of age and cause (Vehicle / Firearm)
    cause_list AS (
        SELECT 'Vehicle' AS "cause"
        UNION ALL
        SELECT 'Firearm'
    ),
    age_cause_grid AS (
        SELECT a."age", c."cause"
        FROM age_series a
        CROSS JOIN cause_list c
    ),

    -- Step 10: Aggregate counts per age and cause
    aggregated AS (
        SELECT
            d."Age" AS "age",
            d."cause",
            COUNT(DISTINCT d."Id") AS "total_deaths",
            COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN d."Race" IN (SELECT "Code" FROM black_race_codes)
                                THEN d."Id" END) AS "black_deaths"
        FROM deaths_with_cause d
        GROUP BY d."Age", d."cause"
    )

-- Step 11: Final output with missing combinations filled as zero
SELECT
    g."age",
    g."cause",
    COALESCE(a."total_deaths", 0) AS "total_deaths",
    COALESCE(a."black_deaths", 0) AS "black_deaths"
FROM age_cause_grid g
LEFT JOIN aggregated a ON g."age" = a."age" AND g."cause" = a."cause"
ORDER BY g."age", g."cause";
```
</details>

<details>
<summary><b>View SlayQL SQL (❌)</b></summary>

```sql
-- Step 1: Define ICD-10 codes whose descriptions contain 'vehicle' or 'firearm'
WITH vehicle_icd_codes AS (
    SELECT DISTINCT "Code"
    FROM DEATH.DEATH.ICD10CODE
    WHERE LOWER("Description") LIKE '%vehicle%'
),
firearm_icd_codes AS (
    SELECT DISTINCT "Code"
    FROM DEATH.DEATH.ICD10CODE
    WHERE LOWER("Description") LIKE '%firearm%'
),

-- Step 2: Identify death records (through EntityAxisConditions) that have at least one such code
vehicle_death_ids AS (
    SELECT DISTINCT eac."DeathRecordId"
    FROM DEATH.DEATH.ENTITYAXISCONDITIONS eac
    INNER JOIN vehicle_icd_codes vic ON eac."Icd10Code" = vic."Code"
),
firearm_death_ids AS (
    SELECT DISTINCT eac."DeathRecordId"
    FROM DEATH.DEATH.ENTITYAXISCONDITIONS eac
    INNER JOIN firearm_icd_codes fic ON eac."Icd10Code" = fic."Code"
),

-- Step 3: For each cause, compute total deaths and Black deaths per age (12-18, age in years)
vehicle_stats AS (
    SELECT
        dr."Age",
        COUNT(DISTINCT dr."Id") AS total_deaths,
        COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN LOWER(r."Description") LIKE '%black%' THEN dr."Id" END) AS black_deaths
    FROM DEATH.DEATH.DEATHRECORDS dr
    INNER JOIN vehicle_death_ids vdi ON dr."Id" = vdi."DeathRecordId"
    LEFT JOIN DEATH.DEATH.RACE r ON dr."Race" = r."Code"
    WHERE dr."AgeType" = 1          -- age in years
      AND dr."Age" BETWEEN 12 AND 18
    GROUP BY dr."Age"
),
firearm_stats AS (
    SELECT
        dr."Age",
        COUNT(DISTINCT dr."Id") AS total_deaths,
        COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN LOWER(r."Description") LIKE '%black%' THEN dr."Id" END) AS black_deaths
    FROM DEATH.DEATH.DEATHRECORDS dr
    INNER JOIN firearm_death_ids fdi ON dr."Id" = fdi."DeathRecordId"
    LEFT JOIN DEATH.DEATH.RACE r ON dr."Race" = r."Code"
    WHERE dr."AgeType" = 1
      AND dr."Age" BETWEEN 12 AND 18
    GROUP BY dr."Age"
)

-- Step 4: Combine and output results with cause label
SELECT
    "Age",
    'vehicle' AS cause,
    "total_deaths",
    "black_deaths"
FROM vehicle_stats
UNION ALL
SELECT
    "Age",
    'firearm' AS cause,
    "total_deaths",
    "black_deaths"
FROM firearm_stats
ORDER BY "Age", cause;
```

#### 📜 Generated SQL Queries

<details>
<summary><b>View Baseline SQL (❌)</b></summary>

```sql
WITH
-- Users who had a session_start in the period
sessions AS (
    SELECT DISTINCT user_pseudo_id
    FROM `firebase-public-project.analytics_153293282.events_*`
    WHERE _TABLE_SUFFIX BETWEEN '20180702' AND '20180716'
      AND event_name = 'session_start'
),

-- For those users, get the earliest quickplay event in the period (first quickplay)
first_quickplay AS (
    SELECT
        s.user_pseudo_id,
        MIN(e.event_timestamp) AS first_qp_timestamp,
        -- Get the event_name of that first quickplay event
        ARRAY_AGG(e.event_name ORDER BY e.event_timestamp LIMIT 1)[OFFSET(0)] AS quickplay_type
    FROM sessions s
    JOIN `firebase-public-project.analytics_153293282.events_*` e
        ON s.user_pseudo_id = e.user_pseudo_id
    WHERE e.event_name LIKE '%_quickplay'
      AND e._TABLE_SUFFIX BETWEEN '20180702' AND '20180716'
    GROUP BY s.user_pseudo_id
),

-- Check retention on day 14 (exactly 14 days after first quickplay)
retained AS (
    SELECT
        fq.user_pseudo_id,
        fq.quickplay_type,
        fq.first_qp_timestamp,
        -- Check if any event exists in the 24-hour window starting 14 days later
        EXISTS(
            SELECT 1
            FROM `firebase-public-project.analytics_153293282.events_*` rt
            WHERE rt.user_pseudo_id = fq.user_pseudo_id
              AND rt.event_timestamp >= fq.first_qp_timestamp + 14 * 86400 * 1000000
              AND rt.event_timestamp < fq.first_qp_timestamp + 15 * 86400 * 1000000
              -- Scan all tables up to July 30 for retention window
              AND rt._TABLE_SUFFIX BETWEEN '20180702' AND '20180730'
        ) AS retained_on_day14
    FROM first_quickplay fq
)

-- Final aggregation: retention rate per quickplay type
SELECT
    quickplay_type,
    COUNT(*) AS total_users,
    SUM(CAST(retained_on_day14 AS INT64)) AS retained_users,
    ROUND(SUM(CAST(retained_on_day14 AS INT64)) / COUNT(*), 4) AS retention_rate
FROM retained
GROUP BY quickplay_type
ORDER BY quickplay_type;
```
</details>

<details>
<summary><b>View SlayQL SQL (❌)</b></summary>

```sql
-- 计算2018年7月2日至7月16日期间，用户首次快速游戏事件后第14天的留存率，按快速游戏事件类型分组
WITH
  -- 1. 筛选出在指定期间内有 session_start 的用户
  users_with_session AS (
    SELECT DISTINCT user_pseudo_id
    FROM `firebase-public-project.analytics_153293282.events_*`
    WHERE event_name = 'session_start'
      AND _TABLE_SUFFIX BETWEEN '20180702' AND '20180716'
  ),
  -- 2. 获取这些用户的所有快速游戏事件（不限日期）
  all_quickplay AS (
    SELECT e.user_pseudo_id, e.event_timestamp, e.event_params, e.event_date
    FROM `firebase-public-project.analytics_153293282.events_*` e
    INNER JOIN users_with_session u
      ON e.user_pseudo_id = u.user_pseudo_id
    WHERE e.event_name = 'quickplay'
  ),
  -- 3. 为每个用户找到最早的一次快速游戏事件，并提取事件类型
  ranked_quickplay AS (
    SELECT user_pseudo_id, event_timestamp, event_date,
      (SELECT value.string_value FROM UNNEST(event_params) WHERE key = 'type') AS quickplay_type,
      ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY user_pseudo_id ORDER BY event_timestamp) AS rn
    FROM all_quickplay
  ),
  first_quickplay AS (
    SELECT user_pseudo_id, event_timestamp, event_date, quickplay_type
    FROM ranked_quickplay
    WHERE rn = 1
      -- 确保首次事件发生在指定期间内
      AND event_date BETWEEN '20180702' AND '20180716'
  ),
  -- 4. 计算每位用户首次事件后的第14天（目标日期）
  target_dates AS (
    SELECT user_pseudo_id, quickplay_type,
      FORMAT_DATE('%Y%m%d', DATE_ADD(PARSE_DATE('%Y%m%d', event_date), INTERVAL 14 DAY)) AS target_date
    FROM first_quickplay
  ),
  -- 5. 判断用户是否在目标日期（第14天）有任何事件（即是否留存）
  retention_flag AS (
    SELECT t.user_pseudo_id, t.quickplay_type,
      EXISTS(
        SELECT 1
        FROM `firebase-public-project.analytics_153293282.events_*` e
        WHERE e.user_pseudo_id = t.user_pseudo_id
          AND e.event_date = t.target_date
          AND _TABLE_SUFFIX = t.target_date   -- 利用分区减少扫描量
      ) AS is_retained
    FROM target_dates t
  )
-- 6. 按快速游戏事件类型汇总并计算留存率
SELECT
  quickplay_type,
  COUNT(DISTINCT user_pseudo_id) AS initial_users,
  COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN is_retained THEN user_pseudo_id END) AS retained_users,
  SAFE_DIVIDE(
    COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN is_retained THEN user_pseudo_id END),
    COUNT(DISTINCT user_pseudo_id)
  ) AS retention_rate
FROM retention_flag
GROUP BY quickplay_type
ORDER BY quickplay_type;
```
</details>

```sql
WITH

            "order_id",
            SUM("payment_value") AS total_payment_per_order
        FROM "order_payments"
        GROUP BY "order_id"
    ),

        SELECT

            COUNT(DISTINCT o."order_id") AS number_of_orders,
            SUM(ops.total_payment_per_order) AS total_payment,
            ROUND(SUM(ops.total_payment_per_order) * 1.0 / COUNT(DISTINCT o."order_id"), 4) AS avg_payment_per_order,

        INNER JOIN "order_payments_sum" ops ON o."order_id" = ops."order_id"
        INNER JOIN "customers" c ON o."customer_id" = c."customer_id"

    ),
    -- Compute lifespan and rank

            ROUND(

                    WHEN julianday(last_purchase) - julianday(first_purchase) < 7 THEN 1.0
                    ELSE (julianday(last_purchase) - julianday(first_purchase)) / 7.0
                END,
                4
            ) AS customer_lifespan_weeks
        FROM customer_metrics
        ORDER BY avg_payment_per_order DESC NULLS LAST

    )
-- Final output
```

```sql
-- Step 1: Compute total payment per order for each customer
WITH order_totals AS (
    SELECT 
        o."customer_id",
        o."order_id",
        o."order_purchase_timestamp",
        SUM(p."payment_value") AS total_payment
    FROM "orders" o
    INNER JOIN "order_payments" p ON o."order_id" = p."order_id"
    GROUP BY o."customer_id", o."order_id", o."order_purchase_timestamp"
),
-- Step 2: Aggregate by customer to get order count, avg payment, and date range
customer_metrics AS (
    SELECT 
        ot."customer_id",
        COUNT(DISTINCT ot."order_id") AS num_orders,
        AVG(ot."total_payment") AS avg_payment_per_order,
        MIN(ot."order_purchase_timestamp") AS first_purchase,
        MAX(ot."order_purchase_timestamp") AS last_purchase
    FROM order_totals ot
    GROUP BY ot."customer_id"
),
-- Step 3: Calculate lifespan in weeks with floor-at-1.0 rule
customer_lifespan AS (
    SELECT 
        "customer_id",
        num_orders,
        avg_payment_per_order,
        CASE 
            WHEN (julianday("last_purchase") - julianday("first_purchase")) / 7.0 < 1.0 
            THEN 1.0
            ELSE (julianday("last_purchase") - julianday("first_purchase")) / 7.0
        END AS lifespan_weeks
    FROM customer_metrics
)
-- Step 4: Return the top 3 customers by highest avg payment per order
SELECT 
    num_orders,
    ROUND(avg_payment_per_order, 4) AS avg_payment,
    ROUND(lifespan_weeks, 4) AS lifespan_weeks
FROM customer_lifespan
ORDER BY avg_payment_per_order DESC NULLS LAST
LIMIT 3;
```

**Question**: Could you help me calculate the average single career span value in years for all baseball players? Please precise the result as a float number. First, calculate the difference in years, months, and days between the debut and final game dates. For each player, the career span is computed as the sum of the absolute number of years, plus the absolute number of months divided by 12, plus the absolute number of days divided by 365. Round each part to two decimal places before summing. Finally, average the career spans and round the result to a float number.

**Status**: Baseline ❌ | SlayQL ❌

#### 📜 Generated SQL Queries

<details>
<summary><b>View Baseline SQL (❌)</b></summary>

```sql
-- Step 1: Compute absolute day difference for each player (debut to final_game)
WITH player_days AS (
    SELECT 
        "player_id",
        ABS(julianday("final_game") - julianday("debut")) AS total_days
    FROM "player"
    WHERE "debut" IS NOT NULL 
      AND "final_game" IS NOT NULL
),
-- Step 2: Approximate years, months, days using 365-day year and 30-day month
player_parts AS (
    SELECT 
        "player_id",
        CAST("total_days" AS INTEGER) / 365   AS years,
        (CAST("total_days" AS INTEGER) % 365) / 30 AS months,
        (CAST("total_days" AS INTEGER) % 365) % 30 AS days
    FROM player_days
),
-- Step 3: Compute career span per player: years + months/12 + days/365, each rounded to 2 decimals
player_span AS (
    SELECT 
        "player_id",
        ROUND(CAST("years" AS REAL), 2) 
        + ROUND(CAST("months" AS REAL) / 12.0, 2) 
        + ROUND(CAST("days" AS REAL) / 365.0, 2) AS career_span
    FROM player_parts
)
-- Step 4: Average all career spans and round final result to 4 decimal places (float)
SELECT ROUND(AVG("career_span"), 4) AS average_career_span
FROM player_span;
```
</details>

<details>
<summary><b>View SlayQL SQL (❌)</b></summary>

```sql
WITH player_date_diff AS (
    SELECT 
        "player_id",
        ABS(CAST(strftime('%Y', "final_game") AS INTEGER) - CAST(strftime('%Y', "debut") AS INTEGER)) AS year_diff,
        ABS(CAST(strftime('%m', "final_game") AS INTEGER) - CAST(strftime('%m', "debut") AS INTEGER)) AS month_diff,
        ABS(CAST(strftime('%d', "final_game") AS INTEGER) - CAST(strftime('%d', "debut") AS INTEGER)) AS day_diff
    FROM "player"
    WHERE "debut" IS NOT NULL AND "final_game" IS NOT NULL 
      AND "debut" != '' AND "final_game" != ''
),
player_career_span AS (
    SELECT 
        "player_id",
        ROUND(CAST(year_diff AS REAL), 2) + 
        ROUND(CAST(month_diff AS REAL) / 12.0, 2) + 
        ROUND(CAST(day_diff AS REAL) / 365.0, 2) AS career_span
    FROM player_date_diff
)
SELECT ROUND(AVG(career_span), 4) AS avg_career_span_years
FROM player_career_span;
```

<details>
<summary><b>View SlayQL SQL (❌)</b></summary>

```sql
-- Step 1: Identify Abakan airport codes using the English city name from the JSON field
WITH
abakan_airports AS (
    SELECT "airport_code"
    FROM "airports_data"
    WHERE json_extract("city", '$.en') = 'Abakan'
),

-- Step 2: Parse coordinates from each airport and convert degrees to radians
airport_coords AS (
    SELECT
        "airport_code",
        (CAST(SUBSTR("coordinates", 2, INSTR("coordinates", ',') - 2) AS REAL) * (3.141592653589793 / 180)) AS "lon_rad",
        (CAST(SUBSTR("coordinates", INSTR("coordinates", ',') + 1, LENGTH("coordinates") - INSTR("coordinates", ',') - 1) AS REAL) * (3.141592653589793 / 180)) AS "lat_rad"
    FROM "airports_data"
),

-- Step 3: Compute Haversine distance for every flight involving Abakan
flight_distances AS (
    SELECT
        f."flight_id",
        2 * 6371 *
        ASIN(
            SQRT(
                POWER(SIN((a2."lat_rad" - a1."lat_rad") / 2), 2) +
                COS(a1."lat_rad") * COS(a2."lat_rad") * POWER(SIN((a2."lon_rad" - a1."lon_rad") / 2), 2)
            )
        ) AS "distance_km"
    FROM "flights" f
    JOIN "airport_coords" a1 ON f."departure_airport" = a1."airport_code"
    JOIN "airport_coords" a2 ON f."arrival_airport" = a2."airport_code"
    WHERE f."departure_airport" IN (SELECT "airport_code" FROM "abakan_airports")
       OR f."arrival_airport" IN (SELECT "airport_code" FROM "abakan_airports")
)

-- Step 4: Return the maximum distance, rounded to 4 decimal places
SELECT ROUND(MAX("distance_km"), 4) AS "longest_route_distance_km"
FROM "flight_distances";
```

<summary><b>View Baseline SQL (❌)</b></summary>

```sql
WITH 
"yearly_total" AS (
    SELECT 
        c2."db_year",
        COUNT(*) AS "total_accidents"
    FROM "collisions" c
    JOIN "case_ids" c2 ON c."case_id" = c2."case_id"
    WHERE c2."db_year" IN (2011, 2021)
    GROUP BY c2."db_year"
),
"category_counts_2021" AS (
    SELECT 
        c."pcf_violation_category",
        COUNT(*) AS "cnt"
    FROM "collisions" c
    JOIN "case_ids" c2 ON c."case_id" = c2."case_id"
    WHERE c2."db_year" = 2021
      AND c."pcf_violation_category" IS NOT NULL
    GROUP BY c."pcf_violation_category"
),
"top_category" AS (
    SELECT 
        "pcf_violation_category"
    FROM "category_counts_2021"
    ORDER BY "cnt" DESC
    LIMIT 1
),
"category_counts" AS (
    SELECT 
        c2."db_year",
        COUNT(*) AS "category_count"
    FROM "collisions" c
    JOIN "case_ids" c2 ON c."case_id" = c2."case_id"
    WHERE c2."db_year" IN (2011, 2021)
      AND c."pcf_violation_category" = (SELECT "pcf_violation_category" FROM "top_category")
    GROUP BY c2."db_year"
)
SELECT 
    ROUND(
        (SELECT "category_count" FROM "category_counts" WHERE "db_year" = 2011) * 100.0 / 
        (SELECT "total_accidents" FROM "yearly_total" WHERE "db_year" = 2011)
        -
        (SELECT "category_count" FROM "category_counts" WHERE "db_year" = 2021) * 100.0 / 
        (SELECT "total_accidents" FROM "yearly_total" WHERE "db_year" = 2021)
        , 4
    ) AS "decrease_percentage_points"
```
</details>

<details>
<summary><b>View SlayQL SQL (❌)</b></summary>

```sql
-- Step 1: Count accidents per pcf_violation_category per year (2011 & 2021)
WITH category_year_counts AS (
    SELECT
        SUBSTR(c."collision_date", 1, 4) AS year,
        c."pcf_violation_category" AS category,
        COUNT(*) AS category_count
    FROM collisions c
    WHERE c."pcf_violation_category" IS NOT NULL
      AND c."pcf_violation_category" != 'None'
      AND SUBSTR(c."collision_date", 1, 4) IN ('2011', '2021')
    GROUP BY SUBSTR(c."collision_date", 1, 4), c."pcf_violation_category"
),

-- Step 2: Total accidents per year (2011 & 2021)
yearly_totals AS (
    SELECT
        SUBSTR(c."collision_date", 1, 4) AS year,
        COUNT(*) AS total_accidents
    FROM collisions c
    WHERE SUBSTR(c."collision_date", 1, 4) IN ('2011', '2021')
    GROUP BY SUBSTR(c."collision_date", 1, 4)
),

-- Step 3: Find the most common pcf_violation_category in 2021
top_category_2021 AS (
    SELECT
        cyc.category
    FROM category_year_counts cyc
    WHERE cyc.year = '2021'
    ORDER BY cyc.category_count DESC
    LIMIT 1
),

-- Step 4: Get shares for the top category in both years
shares AS (
    SELECT
        ROUND(
            SUM(CASE WHEN cyc.year = '2021' THEN cyc.category_count ELSE 0 END) * 100.0
            / MAX(CASE WHEN yt.year = '2021' THEN yt.total_accidents END),
            4
        ) AS share_2021_pct,
        ROUND(
            SUM(CASE WHEN cyc.year = '2011' THEN cyc.category_count ELSE 0 END) * 100.0
            / MAX(CASE WHEN yt.year = '2011' THEN yt.total_accidents END),
            4
        ) AS share_2011_pct
    FROM category_year_counts cyc
    CROSS JOIN yearly_totals yt
    WHERE cyc.category = (SELECT category FROM top_category_2021)
)

-- Step 5: The decrease = share_2011 - share_2021 (positive value if share dropped)
SELECT
    ROUND(share_2011_pct - share_2021_pct, 4) AS percentage_point_decrease
FROM shares;
```
</details>

#### 📜 Generated SQL Queries

<details>
<summary><b>View Baseline SQL (❌)</b></summary>

```sql
-- Find the NXT championship belt with the shortest match (excluding title changes),
-- then retrieve the names of the winner and loser from that match.

WITH
  -- Step 1: Get the promotion ID for NXT
  nxt_promotion AS (
    SELECT id
    FROM "Promotions"
    WHERE name = 'NXT'
  ),
  -- Step 2: Filter matches that belong to NXT events, are for an NXT belt,
  --         have a non‑empty duration, and are not title changes
  nxt_matches AS (
    SELECT m.id, m.winner_id, m.loser_id, m.duration, m.title_id, m.title_change
    FROM "Matches" m
    JOIN "Cards" c ON m.card_id = c.id
    JOIN nxt_promotion p ON c.promotion_id = p.id
    JOIN "Belts" b ON m.title_id = b.id
    WHERE m.title_change = 0                     -- exclude title changes
      AND m.duration != ''                       -- exclude missing durations
      AND LOWER(b.name) LIKE '%nxt%'            -- only NXT championships
  ),
  -- Step 3: Convert the duration (MM:SS) to total seconds for comparison
  match_durations AS (
    SELECT m.*,
           CAST(SUBSTR(m.duration, 1, INSTR(m.duration, ':') - 1) AS INTEGER) * 60 +
           CAST(SUBSTR(m.duration, INSTR(m.duration, ':') + 1) AS INTEGER) AS duration_seconds
    FROM nxt_matches m
  ),
  -- Step 4: Pick the match with the smallest duration (shortest)
  shortest_match AS (
    SELECT * FROM match_durations
    ORDER BY duration_seconds ASC
    LIMIT 1
  )
-- Step 5: Retrieve the names of the two wrestlers involved
SELECT w1.name AS winner_name,
       w2.name AS loser_name
FROM shortest_match sm
JOIN "Wrestlers" w1 ON sm.winner_id = w1.id
JOIN "Wrestlers" w2 ON sm.loser_id = w2.id;
```
</details>

<details>
<summary><b>View SlayQL SQL (❌)</b></summary>

```sql
-- Step 1: Find the NXT promotion ID
WITH nxt_promotion AS (
    SELECT id
    FROM Promotions
    WHERE name = 'NXT'
),

-- Step 2: Find all card IDs belonging to NXT shows
nxt_cards AS (
    SELECT id
    FROM Cards
    WHERE promotion_id IN (SELECT id FROM nxt_promotion)
),

-- Step 3: Get all NXT title matches (excluding title changes) with parsed durations
nxt_title_matches AS (
    SELECT 
        m.id AS match_id,
        m.winner_id,
        m.loser_id,
        b.name AS title_name,
        -- Convert duration from 'MM:SS' format to total seconds
        CAST(SUBSTR(m.duration, 1, 2) AS INTEGER) * 60 + 
        CAST(SUBSTR(m.duration, 4, 2) AS INTEGER) AS duration_seconds
    FROM Matches m
    INNER JOIN Cards c ON m.card_id = c.id
    INNER JOIN Belts b ON m.title_id = b.id
    WHERE c.id IN (SELECT id FROM nxt_cards)
      AND m.title_change = 0          -- Exclude matches where title changed hands
      AND m.duration != ''             -- Only consider matches with recorded duration
      AND b.name LIKE '%NXT%'         -- Only consider NXT-branded titles
),

-- Step 4: Identify the match with the shortest duration
shortest_match AS (
    SELECT 
        winner_id,
        loser_id
    FROM nxt_title_matches
    ORDER BY duration_seconds ASC
    LIMIT 1
)

-- Step 5: Retrieve the names of the two wrestlers involved
SELECT 
    w_winner.name AS winner_name,
    w_loser.name AS loser_name
FROM shortest_match sm
INNER JOIN Wrestlers w_winner ON CAST(sm.winner_id AS INTEGER) = w_winner.id
INNER JOIN Wrestlers w_loser ON CAST(sm.loser_id AS INTEGER) = w_loser.id;
```
</details>

```sql
-- Step 1: Player base information
WITH player_base AS (
    SELECT 
        p."player_id",
        p."player_name",
        p."batting_hand",
        p."bowling_skill"
    FROM "player" p
),

-- Step 2: Most frequent role per player across all matches
role_ranked AS (
    SELECT 
        pm."player_id",
        pm."role",
        COUNT(*) AS role_count,
        ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY pm."player_id" ORDER BY COUNT(*) DESC) AS rn
    FROM "player_match" pm
    GROUP BY pm."player_id", pm."role"
),
player_primary_role AS (
    SELECT 
        r."player_id",
        r."role" AS most_frequent_role
    FROM role_ranked r
    WHERE r.rn = 1
),

-- Step 3: Total matches played per player
matches_played AS (
    SELECT 
        pm."player_id",
        COUNT(DISTINCT pm."match_id") AS total_matches
    FROM "player_match" pm
    GROUP BY pm."player_id"
),

-- Step 4: Batting detail - each ball faced with runs scored
batting_detail AS (
    SELECT 
        bb."striker" AS player_id,
        bb."match_id",
        bb."over_id",
        bb."ball_id",
        bb."innings_no",
        COALESCE(bs."runs_scored", 0) AS runs_scored
    FROM "ball_by_ball" bb
    LEFT JOIN "batsman_scored" bs 
        ON bb."match_id" = bs."match_id" 
        AND bb."over_id" = bs."over_id" 
        AND bb."ball_id" = bs."ball_id" 
        AND bb."innings_no" = bs."innings_no"
),

-- Step 5: Total runs and total balls faced per player
player_batting_totals AS (
    SELECT 
        bd."player_id",
        SUM(bd."runs_scored") AS total_runs,
        COUNT(*) AS total_balls_faced
    FROM batting_detail bd
    GROUP BY bd."player_id"
),

-- Step 6: Total dismissals (each wicket_taken row = one dismissal event)
player_dismissals AS (
    SELECT 
        wt."player_out" AS player_id,
        COUNT(*) AS total_dismissals
    FROM "wicket_taken" wt
    GROUP BY wt."player_out"
),

-- Step 7: Match-level batting scores (summing across innings per match)
match_batting_scores AS (
    SELECT 
        bd."player_id",
        bd."match_id",
        SUM(bd."runs_scored") AS match_runs
    FROM batting_detail bd
    GROUP BY bd."player_id", bd."match_id"
),

-- Step 8: Highest score, matches with 30+, 50+, 100+ runs
batting_match_agg AS (
    SELECT 
        mbs."player_id",
        MAX(mbs."match_runs") AS highest_score,
        SUM(CASE WHEN mbs."match_runs" >= 30 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS matches_ge_30,
        SUM(CASE WHEN mbs."match_runs" >= 50 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS matches_ge_50,
        SUM(CASE WHEN mbs."match_runs" >= 100 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS matches_ge_100
    FROM match_batting_scores mbs
    GROUP BY mbs."player_id"
),

-- Step 9: Bowling detail - each ball bowled with runs conceded
bowling_detail AS (
    SELECT 
        bb."bowler" AS player_id,
        bb."match_id",
        bb."over_id",
        bb."ball_id",
        bb."innings_no",
        COALESCE(bs."runs_scored", 0) AS runs_conceded
    FROM "ball_by_ball" bb
    LEFT JOIN "batsman_scored" bs 
        ON bb."match_id" = bs."match_id" 
        AND bb."over_id" = bs."over_id" 
        AND bb."ball_id" = bs."ball_id" 
        AND bb."innings_no" = bs."innings_no"
),

-- Step 10: Bowling totals (runs conceded, balls bowled)
player_bowling_totals AS (
    SELECT 
        bld."player_id",
        SUM(bld."runs_conceded") AS total_runs_conceded,
        COUNT(*) AS total_balls_bowled
    FROM bowling_detail bld
    GROUP BY bld."player_id"
),

-- Step 11: Total wickets taken as a bowler
bowler_wickets AS (
    SELECT 
        bb."bowler" AS player_id,
        COUNT(*) AS total_wickets
    FROM "ball_by_ball" bb
    INNER JOIN "wicket_taken" wt 
        ON bb."match_id" = wt."match_id" 
        AND bb."over_id" = wt."over_id" 
        AND bb."ball_id" = wt."ball_id" 
        AND bb."innings_no" = wt."innings_no"
    GROUP BY bb."bowler"
),

-- Step 12: Match-level bowling performance
match_bowling_perf AS (
    SELECT 
        bb."bowler" AS player_id,
        bb."match_id",
        COUNT(DISTINCT wt."player_out") AS wickets_in_match,
        SUM(COALESCE(bs."runs_scored", 0)) AS runs_in_match
    FROM "ball_by_ball" bb
    LEFT JOIN "batsman_scored" bs 
        ON bb."match_id" = bs."match_id" 
        AND bb."over_id" = bs."over_id" 
        AND bb."ball_id" = bs."ball_id" 
        AND bb."innings_no" = bs."innings_no"
    LEFT JOIN "wicket_taken" wt 
        ON bb."match_id" = wt."match_id" 
        AND bb."over_id" = wt."over_id" 
        AND bb."ball_id" = wt."ball_id" 
        AND bb."innings_no" = wt."innings_no"
    GROUP BY bb."bowler", bb."match_id"
),

-- Step 13: Best bowling performance (most wickets, fewest runs if tied)
best_bowling_ranked AS (
    SELECT 
        mbp."player_id",
        mbp."wickets_in_match",
        mbp."runs_in_match",
        ROW_NUMBER() OVER (
            PARTITION BY mbp."player_id" 
            ORDER BY mbp."wickets_in_match" DESC, mbp."runs_in_match" ASC
        ) AS rn
    FROM match_bowling_perf mbp
),
best_bowling AS (
    SELECT 
        bbr."player_id",
        CAST(bbr."wickets_in_match" AS TEXT) || '-' || CAST(bbr."runs_in_match" AS TEXT) AS best_bowling_performance
    FROM best_bowling_ranked bbr
    WHERE bbr.rn = 1
)

-- Step 14: Final SELECT combining all statistics per player
SELECT 
    pb."player_id" AS "ID",
    pb."player_name" AS "Name",
    ppr."most_frequent_role" AS "Most Frequent Role",
    pb."batting_hand" AS "Batting Hand",
    pb."bowling_skill" AS "Bowling Skill",
    COALESCE(pbt."total_runs", 0) AS "Total Runs Scored",
    COALESCE(mp."total_matches", 0) AS "Total Matches Played",
    COALESCE(pd."total_dismissals", 0) AS "Total Dismissals",
    CASE 
        WHEN COALESCE(pd."total_dismissals", 0) = 0 THEN NULL
        ELSE ROUND(CAST(COALESCE(pbt."total_runs", 0) AS REAL) / pd."total_dismissals", 4)
    END AS "Batting Average",
    COALESCE(bma."highest_score", 0) AS "Highest Score",
    COALESCE(bma."matches_ge_30", 0) AS "Matches >= 30 Runs",
    COALESCE(bma."matches_ge_50", 0) AS "Matches >= 50 Runs",
    COALESCE(bma."matches_ge_100", 0) AS "Matches >= 100 Runs",
    COALESCE(pbt."total_balls_faced", 0) AS "Total Balls Faced",
    CASE 
        WHEN COALESCE(pbt."total_balls_faced", 0) = 0 THEN NULL
        ELSE ROUND(CAST(COALESCE(pbt."total_runs", 0) AS REAL) / pbt."total_balls_faced" * 100.0, 4)
    END AS "Strike Rate",
    COALESCE(bw."total_wickets", 0) AS "Total Wickets Taken",
    CASE 
        WHEN COALESCE(pblt."total_balls_bowled", 0) = 0 THEN NULL
        ELSE ROUND(CAST(COALESCE(pblt."total_runs_conceded", 0) AS REAL) / pblt."total_balls_bowled" * 6.0, 4)
    END AS "Economy Rate",
    COALESCE(bbp."best_bowling_performance', '0-0') AS "Best Bowling Performance"
FROM player_base pb
LEFT JOIN player_primary_role ppr ON pb."player_id" = ppr."player_id"
LEFT JOIN matches_played mp ON pb."player_id" = mp."player_id"
LEFT JOIN player_batting_totals pbt ON pb."player_id" = pbt."player_id"
LEFT JOIN player_dismissals pd ON pb."player_id" = pd."player_id"
LEFT JOIN batting_match_agg bma ON pb."player_id" = bma."player_id"
LEFT JOIN player_bowling_totals pblt ON pb."player_id" = pblt."player_id"
LEFT JOIN bowler_wickets bw ON pb."player_id" = bw."player_id"
LEFT JOIN best_bowling bbp ON pb."player_id" = bbp."player_id"
ORDER BY pb."player_id";
```

```sql
-- CTE to compute total extras per ball (since extra_runs table may have multiple rows per ball)
WITH extra_by_ball AS (
    SELECT
        match_id,
        innings_no,
        over_id,
        ball_id,
        SUM(extra_runs) AS extra_total
    FROM extra_runs
    GROUP BY match_id, innings_no, over_id, ball_id
),
-- Enrich each ball with runs scored and extras
ball_data AS (
    SELECT
        b.match_id,
        b.innings_no,
        b.over_id,
        b.ball_id,
        b.striker,
        b.non_striker,
        COALESCE(bs.runs_scored, 0) AS runs_scored,
        COALESCE(e.extra_total, 0) AS extra_runs
    FROM ball_by_ball b
    LEFT JOIN batsman_scored bs
        ON b.match_id = bs.match_id
        AND b.innings_no = bs.innings_no
        AND b.over_id = bs.over_id
        AND b.ball_id = bs.ball_id
    LEFT JOIN extra_by_ball e
        ON b.match_id = e.match_id
        AND b.innings_no = e.innings_no
        AND b.over_id = e.over_id
        AND b.ball_id = e.ball_id
),
-- Aggregate by match and unordered player pair
partnership_agg AS (
    SELECT
        match_id,
        MIN(striker, non_striker) AS player1,   -- smaller ID
        MAX(striker, non_striker) AS player2,   -- larger ID
        SUM(runs_scored) + SUM(extra_runs) AS partnership_total,
        -- Individual runs when the player is the striker
        SUM(CASE WHEN striker < non_striker THEN runs_scored ELSE 0 END) AS individual1,
        SUM(CASE WHEN striker > non_striker THEN runs_scored ELSE 0 END) AS individual2
    FROM ball_data
    GROUP BY match_id, player1, player2
),
-- Rank partnerships per match by total runs
ranked AS (
    SELECT
        match_id,
        player1,
        player2,
        individual1,
        individual2,
        partnership_total,
        RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY match_id ORDER BY partnership_total DESC) AS rnk
    FROM partnership_agg
)
-- Final output: reorder players by individual score (desc), then by player ID (desc) in case of tie
SELECT
    match_id,
    CASE
        WHEN individual1 > individual2 THEN player1
        WHEN individual2 > individual1 THEN player2
        ELSE player2   -- if individual scores equal, higher ID becomes player1
    END AS player_id_1,
    CASE
        WHEN individual1 > individual2 THEN player2
        WHEN individual2 > individual1 THEN player1
        ELSE player1
    END AS player_id_2,
    CASE
        WHEN individual1 > individual2 THEN individual1
        WHEN individual2 > individual1 THEN individual2
        ELSE individual2   -- player1' score = individual2 (since player2 has higher ID)
    END AS individual_score_1,
    CASE
        WHEN individual1 > individual2 THEN individual2
        WHEN individual2 > individual1 THEN individual1
        ELSE individual1
    END AS individual_score_2,
    partnership_total
FROM ranked
WHERE rnk = 1
ORDER BY match_id, player_id_1; -- order for readability
```

<details>
<summary><b>View SlayQL SQL (❌)</b></summary>

```sql
WITH ball_data AS (
    -- Join ball_by_ball with batsman_scored to associate runs with striker/non_striker
    SELECT 
        b.match_id,
        b.striker,
        b.non_striker,
        COALESCE(bs.runs_scored, 0) AS runs_scored
    FROM ball_by_ball b
    LEFT JOIN batsman_scored bs
        ON b.match_id = bs.match_id
        AND b.innings_no = bs.innings_no
        AND b.over_id = bs.over_id
        AND b.ball_id = bs.ball_id
),
individual_scores AS (
    -- Total runs scored by each player in each match (as striker)
    SELECT 
        match_id,
        striker AS player_id,
        SUM(runs_scored) AS individual_score
    FROM ball_data
    GROUP BY match_id, striker
),
partnerships AS (
    -- For each unordered pair of players in each match, sum the partnership runs
    SELECT 
        match_id,
        LEAST(striker, non_striker) AS player_a,
        GREATEST(striker, non_striker) AS player_b,
        SUM(runs_scored) AS partnership_runs
    FROM ball_data
    GROUP BY match_id, LEAST(striker, non_striker), GREATEST(striker, non_striker)
),
ranked_partnerships AS (
    -- Rank partnerships within each match by total partnership runs descending
    SELECT 
        p.*,
        RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY p.match_id ORDER BY p.partnership_runs DESC) AS rnk
    FROM partnerships p
),
top_partnerships AS (
    -- Keep only the top-ranked (highest partnership runs) for each match
    SELECT 
        rp.match_id,
        rp.player_a,
        rp.player_b,
        rp.partnership_runs,
        COALESCE(i1.individual_score, 0) AS score_a,
        COALESCE(i2.individual_score, 0) AS score_b
    FROM ranked_partnerships rp
    LEFT JOIN individual_scores i1 
        ON rp.match_id = i1.match_id AND rp.player_a = i1.player_id
    LEFT JOIN individual_scores i2
        ON rp.match_id = i2.match_id AND rp.player_b = i2.player_id
    WHERE rp.rnk = 1
)
-- Final output with proper ordering: player1 has higher individual score
-- (or higher ID if scores are equal)
SELECT 
    CASE 
        WHEN score_a > score_b THEN player_a
        WHEN score_b > score_a THEN player_b
        WHEN player_a > player_b THEN player_a
        ELSE player_b
    END AS player1_id,
    CASE 
        WHEN score_a > score_b THEN player_b
        WHEN score_b > score_a THEN player_a
        WHEN player_a > player_b THEN player_b
        ELSE player_a
    END AS player2_id,
    CASE 
        WHEN score_a > score_b THEN score_a
        WHEN score_b > score_a THEN score_b
        WHEN player_a > player_b THEN score_a
        ELSE score_b
    END AS player1_score,
    CASE 
        WHEN score_a > score_b THEN score_b
        WHEN score_b > score_a THEN score_a
        WHEN player_a > player_b THEN score_b
        ELSE score_a
    END AS player2_score,
    partnership_runs
FROM top_partnerships
ORDER BY match_id;
```

### 120. local031 (DB: `Brazilian_E_Commerce`)
**Question**: What is the highest monthly delivered orders volume in the year with the lowest annual delivered orders volume among 2016, 2017, and 2018?

```sql
-- Step 1: Extract year and month from delivery dates for delivered orders in 2016-2018
WITH delivered_orders AS (
    SELECT 
        "order_id",
        CAST(strftime('%Y', "order_delivered_customer_date") AS INTEGER) AS "year",
        CAST(strftime('%m', "order_delivered_customer_date") AS INTEGER) AS "month"
    FROM "olist_orders"
    WHERE "order_status" = 'delivered'
      AND "order_delivered_customer_date" IS NOT NULL
      AND CAST(strftime('%Y', "order_delivered_customer_date") AS INTEGER) IN (2016, 2017, 2018)
),

-- Step 2: Compute annual delivered orders volume
annual_volumes AS (
    SELECT 
        "year",
        COUNT("order_id") AS "annual_volume"
    FROM delivered_orders
    GROUP BY "year"
),

-- Step 3: Identify the year with the lowest annual volume
lowest_year AS (
    SELECT "year"
    FROM annual_volumes
    ORDER BY "annual_volume" ASC
    LIMIT 1
),

-- Step 4: Compute monthly volumes for that year
monthly_volumes AS (
    SELECT 
        "month",
        COUNT("order_id") AS "monthly_volume"
    FROM delivered_orders
    WHERE "year" = (SELECT "year" FROM lowest_year)
    GROUP BY "month"
)

-- Step 5: Get the highest monthly volume
SELECT MAX("monthly_volume") AS "highest_monthly_delivered_orders_volume"
FROM monthly_volumes;
```
</details>

<details>
<summary><b>View SlayQL SQL (❌)</b></summary>

```sql
WITH 
-- Extract year and month for delivered orders in 2016-2018
delivered_orders AS (
    SELECT 
        order_id,
        SUBSTR(order_delivered_customer_date, 1, 4) AS year,
        SUBSTR(order_delivered_customer_date, 6, 2) AS month
    FROM olist_orders
    WHERE order_status = 'delivered'
      AND order_delivered_customer_date IS NOT NULL
      AND SUBSTR(order_delivered_customer_date, 1, 4) IN ('2016', '2017', '2018')
),
-- Count annual delivered orders volume
annual_volumes AS (
    SELECT 
        year,
        COUNT(*) AS annual_count
    FROM delivered_orders
    GROUP BY year
),
-- Identify the year with the lowest annual volume
lowest_volume_year AS (
    SELECT year
    FROM annual_volumes
    ORDER BY annual_count ASC
    LIMIT 1
),
-- Count monthly delivered orders for that specific year
monthly_volumes AS (
    SELECT 
        year,
        month,
        COUNT(*) AS monthly_count
    FROM delivered_orders
    WHERE year = (SELECT year FROM lowest_volume_year)
    GROUP BY year, month
)
-- Return the highest monthly volume
SELECT MAX(monthly_count) AS highest_monthly_delivered_orders_volume
```

```sql
-- Step 1: Identify films matching all criteria: English language, Children category, rating G or PG, length <= 120, release year between 2000 and 2010.
-- Step 2: Join film_actor and actor to count appearances per actor.
-- Step 3: Order by count descending and take the top actor. Provide full name.

WITH qualified_films AS (
    SELECT f.film_id
    FROM "film" f
    JOIN "language" l ON f.language_id = l.language_id
    JOIN "film_category" fc ON f.film_id = fc.film_id
    JOIN "category" c ON fc.category_id = c.category_id
    WHERE l.name = 'English'
      AND c.name = 'Children'
      AND f.rating IN ('G', 'PG')
      AND f.length <= 120
      AND CAST(f.release_year AS INTEGER) BETWEEN 2000 AND 2010
),
actor_counts AS (
    SELECT fa.actor_id,
           COUNT(*) AS film_count
    FROM "film_actor" fa
    JOIN qualified_films qf ON fa.film_id = qf.film_id
    GROUP BY fa.actor_id
)
SELECT a.first_name || ' ' || a.last_name AS actor_full_name
FROM actor_counts ac
JOIN "actor" a ON ac.actor_id = a.actor_id
ORDER BY ac.film_count DESC
LIMIT 1;
```

<details>
<summary><b>View SlayQL SQL (❌)</b></summary>

```sql
WITH 
    -- Identify the English language ID from the language lookup table
    english_language AS (
        SELECT language_id 
        FROM language 
        WHERE name = 'English'
    ),
    -- Films satisfying: English language, G or PG rating, ≤120 minutes, released 2000-2010
    base_films AS (
        SELECT f.film_id
        FROM film f
        CROSS JOIN english_language el
        WHERE f.language_id = el.language_id
          AND f.rating IN ('G', 'PG')
          AND f.length <= 120
          AND CAST(f.release_year AS INTEGER) BETWEEN 2000 AND 2010
    ),
    -- Films belonging to the 'Children' category
    children_films AS (
        SELECT fc.film_id
        FROM film_category fc
        JOIN category c ON fc.category_id = c.category_id
        WHERE c.name = 'Children'
    ),
    -- Intersection: English-language children's films meeting all criteria
    qualified_films AS (
        SELECT bf.film_id
        FROM base_films bf
        INNER JOIN children_films cf ON bf.film_id = cf.film_id
    ),
    -- Count how many qualified films each actor appeared in
    actor_appearances AS (
        SELECT fa.actor_id, COUNT(*) AS appearance_count
        FROM film_actor fa
        INNER JOIN qualified_films qf ON fa.film_id = qf.film_id
        GROUP BY fa.actor_id
    ),
    -- Select the actor with the highest appearance count
    top_actor AS (
        SELECT actor_id
        FROM actor_appearances
        ORDER BY appearance_count DESC
        LIMIT 1
    )
-- Return the full name of the top actor
SELECT a.first_name || ' ' || a.last_name AS actor_full_name
FROM actor a
INNER JOIN top_actor ta ON a.actor_id = ta.actor_id;
```

```sql
-- Step 1: Identify unicorn companies with their founding year and industry
WITH unicorn_companies AS (
    SELECT
        cd.company_id,
        cd.date_joined,
        ci.industry
    FROM companies_dates cd
    JOIN companies_funding cf ON cd.company_id = cf.company_id
    JOIN companies_industries ci ON cd.company_id = ci.company_id
    WHERE cf.valuation >= 1000000000  -- Unicorn threshold: $1B
      AND strftime('%Y', cd.date_joined) BETWEEN '2019' AND '2021'
),
-- Step 2: Count new unicorns per industry per year
counts_per_industry_year AS (
    SELECT
        industry,
        strftime('%Y', date_joined) AS year,
        COUNT(DISTINCT company_id) AS cnt
    FROM unicorn_companies
    GROUP BY industry, year
),
-- Step 3: Sum counts across 2019-2021 for each industry to find the top
total_counts_per_industry AS (
    SELECT
        industry,
        SUM(cnt) AS total_count
    FROM counts_per_industry_year
    GROUP BY industry
),
-- Step 4: Identify the top industry (highest total count; if tie, pick alphabetically)
top_industry AS (
    SELECT industry
    FROM total_counts_per_industry
    ORDER BY total_count DESC, industry ASC
    LIMIT 1
)
-- Step 5: Compute average new unicorns per year for the top industry (2019-2021)
SELECT ROUND(SUM(cnt) / 3.0, 4) AS avg_new_unicorns_per_year
FROM counts_per_industry_year
WHERE industry = (SELECT industry FROM top_industry)
  AND year BETWEEN '2019' AND '2021';
```
</details>

```sql
WITH unicorn_yearly AS (
    SELECT 
        ci.industry,
        SUBSTR(cd.date_joined, 1, 4) AS year,
        COUNT(DISTINCT cd.company_id) AS cnt
    FROM companies_dates cd
    JOIN companies_industries ci ON cd.company_id = ci.company_id
    WHERE SUBSTR(cd.date_joined, 1, 4) BETWEEN '2019' AND '2021'
    GROUP BY ci.industry, SUBSTR(cd.date_joined, 1, 4)
),
industry_total AS (
    SELECT 
        industry,
        SUM(cnt) AS total_unicorns,
        COUNT(DISTINCT year) AS num_years
    FROM unicorn_yearly
    GROUP BY industry
),
top_industry AS (
    SELECT industry
    FROM industry_total
    ORDER BY total_unicorns DESC NULLS LAST
    LIMIT 1
)
SELECT 
    ROUND(AVG(cnt), 4) AS avg_new_unicorns_per_year
FROM unicorn_yearly
WHERE industry IN (SELECT industry FROM top_industry);
```

**Status**: Baseline ❌ | SlayQL ❌

#### 📊 Execution Results Comparison

#### 📜 Generated SQL Queries

<details>
<summary><b>View Baseline SQL (❌)</b></summary>


<details>
<summary><b>View SlayQL SQL (❌)</b></summary>

```sql
-- This query finds, for each rating category of the first movie rented by a customer,
-- the average total amount spent per customer and the average number of subsequent rentals.
-- The first movie is determined by the earliest payment date per customer (with tiebreaker by payment_id).

WITH
    -- 1. Identify the first payment per customer (earliest payment_date, break ties with payment_id)
    first_payment AS (
        SELECT
            "customer_id",
            "payment_id",
            "rental_id",
            "payment_date",
            ROW_NUMBER() OVER (
                PARTITION BY "customer_id"
                ORDER BY "payment_date", "payment_id"
            ) AS "rn"
        FROM "payment"
    ),
    -- 2. Get the film rating for that first rental
    customer_first_rental AS (
        SELECT
            fp."customer_id",
            f."rating"
        FROM first_payment fp
        JOIN "rental" r ON fp."rental_id" = r."rental_id"
        JOIN "inventory" i ON r."inventory_id" = i."inventory_id"
        JOIN "film" f ON i."film_id" = f."film_id"
        WHERE fp."rn" = 1
    ),
    -- 3. Aggregate total amount spent per customer from all payments
    customer_total_spent AS (
        SELECT
            "customer_id",
            SUM("amount") AS "total_spent"
        FROM "payment"
        GROUP BY "customer_id"
    ),
    -- 4. Count total rentals per customer
    customer_total_rentals AS (
        SELECT
            "customer_id",
            COUNT(*) AS "total_rentals"
        FROM "rental"
        GROUP BY "customer_id"
    )
-- 5. Compute averages per rating category
SELECT
    cfr."rating",
    ROUND(AVG(cts."total_spent"), 4) AS "avg_total_amount_spent",
    ROUND(AVG(ctr."total_rentals" - 1), 4) AS "avg_subsequent_rentals"
FROM customer_first_rental cfr
JOIN customer_total_spent cts ON cfr."customer_id" = cts."customer_id"
JOIN customer_total_rentals ctr ON cfr."customer_id" = ctr."customer_id"
GROUP BY cfr."rating"
ORDER BY cfr."rating";
```
</details>

```sql
WITH 
-- Clean salary values: remove currency symbol, commas, convert monthly to annual
cleaned_salaries AS (
    SELECT 
        "Location",
        "CompanyName",
        CASE 
            WHEN "Salary" LIKE '%/mo' THEN 
                CAST(REPLACE(REPLACE(REPLACE("Salary", '₹', ''), ',', ''), '/mo', '') AS REAL) * 12
            ELSE 
                CAST(REPLACE(REPLACE(REPLACE("Salary", '₹', ''), ',', ''), '/yr', '') AS REAL)
        END AS annual_salary
    FROM "SalaryDataset"
    WHERE "Location" IN ('Mumbai', 'Pune', 'New Delhi', 'Hyderabad')
),
-- Average salary per company per city
city_company_avg AS (
    SELECT 
        "Location",
        "CompanyName",
        ROUND(AVG("annual_salary"), 4) AS avg_salary_in_state
    FROM cleaned_salaries
    GROUP BY "Location", "CompanyName"
),
-- National average across all four cities
national_avg AS (
    SELECT ROUND(AVG("annual_salary"), 4) AS avg_salary_in_country
    FROM cleaned_salaries
),
-- Rank companies within each city by average salary descending
ranked_companies AS (
    SELECT 
        cca."Location",
        cca."CompanyName",
        cca.avg_salary_in_state,
        na.avg_salary_in_country,
        ROW_NUMBER() OVER (
            PARTITION BY cca."Location" 
            ORDER BY cca.avg_salary_in_state DESC NULLS LAST
        ) AS rank
    FROM city_company_avg cca
    CROSS JOIN national_avg na
)
-- Final output: top 5 per location
SELECT 
    "Location",
    "CompanyName",
    avg_salary_in_state AS "Average Salary in State",
    avg_salary_in_country AS "Average Salary in Country"
FROM ranked_companies
WHERE rank <= 5
ORDER BY "Location", rank;
```

```sql
-- ============================================================
-- Step 1: Clean Salary data by removing non-numeric characters
-- and converting to annual numeric salary
-- ============================================================
WITH cleaned_salaries AS (
    SELECT
        "Location",
        "CompanyName",
        CASE
            -- If salary is monthly (contains '/mo'), multiply by 12 to annualize
            WHEN "Salary" LIKE '%/mo' THEN
                CAST(
                    REPLACE(
                        REPLACE(
                            REPLACE(
                                REPLACE("Salary", '₹', ''),
                            ',', ''),
                        '/mo', ''),
                    '/yr', '')
                AS REAL) * 12
            -- If salary is yearly ('/yr') or other, use as-is
            ELSE
                CAST(
                    REPLACE(
                        REPLACE(
                            REPLACE(
                                REPLACE("Salary", '₹', ''),
                            ',', ''),
                        '/mo', ''),
                    '/yr', '')
                AS REAL)
        END AS "AnnualSalary"
    FROM "SalaryDataset"
),

-- ============================================================
-- Step 2: Compute the overall national average salary
-- (using ALL locations, not just the 4 target cities)
-- ============================================================
national_average AS (
    SELECT
        AVG("AnnualSalary") AS "NationalAvgSalary"
    FROM "cleaned_salaries"
),

-- ============================================================
-- Step 3: Filter to only the 4 target cities
-- ============================================================
target_city_salaries AS (
    SELECT
        "Location",
        "CompanyName",
        "AnnualSalary"
    FROM "cleaned_salaries"
    WHERE "Location" IN ('Mumbai', 'Pune', 'New Delhi', 'Hyderabad')
),

-- ============================================================
-- Step 4: Calculate average salary per company per city
-- ============================================================
city_company_averages AS (
    SELECT
        "Location",
        "CompanyName",
        AVG("AnnualSalary") AS "AvgSalaryInCity"
    FROM "target_city_salaries"
    GROUP BY "Location", "CompanyName"
),

-- ============================================================
-- Step 5: Join with national average and rank companies
-- within each city by descending average salary
-- ============================================================
ranked_companies AS (
    SELECT
        c."Location",
        c."CompanyName",
        ROUND(c."AvgSalaryInCity", 4)          AS "Average Salary in State",
        ROUND(n."NationalAvgSalary", 4)        AS "Average Salary in Country",
        ROW_NUMBER() OVER (
            PARTITION BY c."Location"
            ORDER BY c."AvgSalaryInCity" DESC  NULLS LAST
        ) AS "rank"
    FROM "city_company_averages" c
    CROSS JOIN "national_average" n
)

-- ============================================================
-- Step 6: Final output — top 5 companies per city
-- ============================================================
SELECT
    "Location",
    "CompanyName"                                AS "Company Name",
    "Average Salary in State",
    "Average Salary in Country"
FROM "ranked_companies"
WHERE "rank" <= 5
ORDER BY
    "Location",
    "rank";
```

```sql
-- Step 1: Filter sales for France, promo_total_id=1, channel_total_id=1, years 2019/2020
WITH filtered_sales AS (
    SELECT
        s."prod_id",
        t."calendar_month_number" AS "month",
        t."calendar_year" AS "year",
        s."amount_sold"
    FROM "sales" AS s
    JOIN "times" AS t ON s."time_id" = t."time_id"
    JOIN "customers" AS c ON s."cust_id" = c."cust_id"
    JOIN "countries" AS co ON c."country_id" = co."country_id"
    JOIN "promotions" AS p ON s."promo_id" = p."promo_id"
    JOIN "channels" AS ch ON s."channel_id" = ch."channel_id"
    WHERE LOWER(co."country_name") = LOWER('France')
      AND p."promo_total_id" = 1
      AND ch."channel_total_id" = 1
      AND t."calendar_year" IN (2019, 2020)
),
-- Step 2: Aggregate sales per product, month, year
agg_sales AS (
    SELECT
        "prod_id",
        "month",
        "year",
        SUM("amount_sold") AS "total_sales"
    FROM filtered_sales
    GROUP BY "prod_id", "month", "year"
),
-- Step 3: Pivot to get sales for 2019 and 2020 per product-month
pivot_sales AS (
    SELECT
        "prod_id",
        "month",
        MAX(CASE WHEN "year" = 2019 THEN "total_sales" END) AS "sales_2019",
        MAX(CASE WHEN "year" = 2020 THEN "total_sales" END) AS "sales_2020"
    FROM agg_sales
    GROUP BY "prod_id", "month"
),
-- Step 4: Project 2021 sales using the given growth formula
projected AS (
    SELECT
        "prod_id",
        "month",
        CASE
            WHEN "sales_2019" IS NOT NULL AND "sales_2019" > 0
            THEN ((("sales_2020" - "sales_2019") / "sales_2019") * "sales_2020") + "sales_2020"
            ELSE NULL
        END AS "projected_sales_local"
    FROM pivot_sales
),
-- Step 5: Convert to USD using currency rates for France, year=2021
projected_usd AS (
    SELECT
        pr."prod_id",
        pr."month",
        ROUND(pr."projected_sales_local" * COALESCE(cr."to_us", 1), 2) AS "projected_sales_usd"
    FROM projected AS pr
    LEFT JOIN "currency" AS cr
        ON cr."month" = pr."month"
        AND cr."year" = 2021
        AND LOWER(cr."country") = LOWER('France')
    WHERE pr."projected_sales_local" IS NOT NULL  -- exclude invalid projections (division by zero)
),
-- Step 6: Compute monthly averages across all products
monthly_avg AS (
    SELECT
        "month",
        ROUND(AVG("projected_sales_usd"), 2) AS "avg_monthly_sales"
    FROM projected_usd
    GROUP BY "month"
),
-- Step 7: Calculate median of the twelve monthly averages
median_calc AS (
    SELECT
        "avg_monthly_sales",
        ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY "avg_monthly_sales") AS "rn",
        COUNT(*) OVER () AS "cnt"
    FROM monthly_avg
)
SELECT ROUND(AVG("avg_monthly_sales"), 2) AS "median_of_monthly_avg_projected_sales_usd"
FROM median_calc
WHERE "rn" IN (("cnt" + 1) / 2, ("cnt" + 2) / 2);
```
</details>

<details>
<summary><b>View SlayQL SQL (❌)</b></summary>

```sql
-- Step 1: Monthly sales in 2019 (France, promo_total_id=1, channel_total_id=1)
WITH sales_2019 AS (
    SELECT 
        s.prod_id,
        t.calendar_month_number AS month,
        SUM(s.amount_sold) AS total_sales
    FROM sales s
    JOIN times t ON s.time_id = t.time_id
    JOIN promotions p ON s.promo_id = p.promo_id
    JOIN channels ch ON s.channel_id = ch.channel_id
    JOIN customers c ON s.cust_id = c.cust_id
    JOIN countries co ON c.country_id = co.country_id
    WHERE t.calendar_year = 2019
        AND p.promo_total_id = 1
        AND ch.channel_total_id = 1
        AND co.country_name = 'France'
    GROUP BY s.prod_id, t.calendar_month_number
),
-- Step 2: Monthly sales in 2020 (same filters)
sales_2020 AS (
    SELECT 
        s.prod_id,
        t.calendar_month_number AS month,
        SUM(s.amount_sold) AS total_sales
    FROM sales s
    JOIN times t ON s.time_id = t.time_id
    JOIN promotions p ON s.promo_id = p.promo_id
    JOIN channels ch ON s.channel_id = ch.channel_id
    JOIN customers c ON s.cust_id = c.cust_id
    JOIN countries co ON c.country_id = co.country_id
    WHERE t.calendar_year = 2020
        AND p.promo_total_id = 1
        AND ch.channel_total_id = 1
        AND co.country_name = 'France'
    GROUP BY s.prod_id, t.calendar_month_number
),
-- Step 3: Project 2021 sales per product/month using growth rate from 2019->2020
projected AS (
    SELECT 
        a.prod_id,
        a.month,
        -- Formula: ((2020sales - 2019sales) / 2019sales) * 2020sales + 2020sales = 2020sales^2 / 2019sales
        CASE 
            WHEN a.total_sales IS NOT NULL AND a.total_sales != 0 
                 AND b.total_sales IS NOT NULL AND b.total_sales != 0 
            THEN (b.total_sales * b.total_sales) / a.total_sales
            ELSE NULL
        END AS projected_sales
    FROM sales_2019 a
    JOIN sales_2020 b ON a.prod_id = b.prod_id AND a.month = b.month
),
-- Step 4: Convert projected sales to USD using currency table (2021 rates)
converted AS (
    SELECT 
        p.month,
        p.projected_sales * COALESCE(cur.to_us, 1) AS projected_usd
    FROM projected p
    LEFT JOIN currency cur ON cur.country = 'France' 
        AND cur.year = 2021 
        AND cur.month = p.month
    WHERE p.projected_sales IS NOT NULL
),
-- Step 5: Average projected sales per month (across products)
monthly_avg AS (
    SELECT 
        month,
        AVG(projected_usd) AS avg_projected
    FROM converted
    GROUP BY month
),
-- Step 6: Compute median of the 12 monthly averages
median AS (
    SELECT 
        AVG(avg_projected) AS median_val
    FROM (
        SELECT 
            avg_projected,
            ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY avg_projected) AS rn,
            COUNT(*) OVER () AS cnt
        FROM monthly_avg
    )
    WHERE rn IN ((cnt + 1) / 2, (cnt + 2) / 2)
)
SELECT median_val FROM median;
```
</details>

```sql
-- Step 1: Compute per-state alien statistics (total, friendly, hostile, average age)
WITH state_stats AS (
    SELECT
        "state",
        COUNT(*) AS total_aliens,
        SUM(CASE WHEN "aggressive" = 0 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS friendly_count,
        SUM(CASE WHEN "aggressive" = 1 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS hostile_count,
        AVG("age") AS avg_age
    FROM "alien_data"
    GROUP BY "state"
),
-- Step 2: Rank states by total alien population descending
ranked_states AS (
    SELECT
        "state",
        total_aliens,
        friendly_count,
        hostile_count,
        avg_age,
        ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY total_aliens DESC) AS rn
    FROM state_stats
)
-- Step 3 & 4: Filter top 10, apply conditions, count matching states
SELECT COUNT(*) AS matching_states_count
FROM ranked_states
WHERE rn <= 10
  AND friendly_count > hostile_count   -- friendly percentage > hostile percentage
  AND avg_age > 200;
```

```sql
    GROUP BY "state"

    LIMIT 10
),

        ad."state",

    FROM "alien_data" ad
```

```sql
WITH filtered_jobs AS (

    FROM filtered_jobs fj

FROM final_jobs;
```

```sql
WITH
-- Step 1: Filter to remote Data Analyst jobs with non-null annual salary
qualified_jobs AS (
    SELECT
        job_id,
        salary_year_avg
    FROM job_postings_fact
    WHERE job_title_short = 'Data Analyst'
      AND salary_year_avg IS NOT NULL
      AND job_work_from_home = 1
),
-- Step 2: Count how many qualified job postings demand each skill
skill_frequencies AS (
    SELECT
        sjd.skill_id,
        sd.skills,
        COUNT(*) AS freq
    FROM qualified_jobs qj
    JOIN skills_job_dim sjd ON qj.job_id = sjd.job_id
    JOIN skills_dim sd ON sjd.skill_id = sd.skill_id
    GROUP BY sjd.skill_id, sd.skills
),
-- Step 3: Identify the top 3 most frequently demanded skills
top_skills AS (
    SELECT skill_id
    FROM skill_frequencies
    ORDER BY freq DESC NULLS LAST
    LIMIT 3
),
-- Step 4: Find all qualified jobs that require at least one of the top 3 skills
jobs_with_top_skills AS (
    SELECT DISTINCT qj.job_id, qj.salary_year_avg
    FROM qualified_jobs qj
    JOIN skills_job_dim sjd ON qj.job_id = sjd.job_id
    JOIN top_skills ts ON sjd.skill_id = ts.skill_id
)
-- Step 5: Calculate the overall average salary across these positions
SELECT ROUND(AVG(salary_year_avg), 4) AS overall_avg_salary
FROM jobs_with_top_skills;
```

**Question**: For veg whsle data, can you generate a summary of our items' loss rates? Include the average loss rate, and also break down the count of items that are below, above, and within one standard deviation from this average.

**Status**: Baseline ❌ | SlayQL ❌

#### 📊 Execution Results Comparison

<details open>

|   AVG_LOSS_RATE |   COUNT_BELOW |   COUNT_WITHIN |   COUNT_ABOVE |

|   BELOW_COUNT |   WITHIN_COUNT |   ABOVE_COUNT |   AVG_LOSS |   STDEV_LOSS |
|--------------:|---------------:|--------------:|-----------:|-------------:|
|            35 |            187 |            29 |    9.42669 |      5.20064 |

N/A
